items.title: multi-db: feature-parity audit + multi-tenancy schema-isolation on MySQL and SQL Server
items.body:
## Summary

Two related multi-database gaps. **First**, the v2.3.2 dialect crates (`crates/fraiseql-db/src/dialect/{postgres,mysql,sqlite,sqlserver}.rs`) compile against all four databases, but there is no published per-DB × per-feature parity matrix. Adopters with non-PostgreSQL workloads cannot tell from the docs whether subscriptions, RLS, schema-isolation, native aggregations, JSON operators, LTree, partial-period, or full-text-search work end-to-end on their database of choice. **Second**, multi-tenancy `schema` isolation mode is documented as PostgreSQL-only (`SET search_path` is PG-specific). MySQL has an analogous "database-per-tenant" isolation pattern (`USE tenant_acme`); SQL Server has schema-per-tenant via `EXEC sp_set_session_context`. Neither is wired today.

## Why

- **Adoption-blocker for mixed fleets.** Enterprises with MySQL or MSSQL workloads need clarity on what works.
- **The multi-DB story is a differentiator** — but only if it's verified end-to-end, not just at compile time.
- **Multi-tenancy is non-trivial to add per-DB** — adopters who pick MySQL or MSSQL today get row-isolation mode only, which often isn't strong enough for regulated workloads.

## Current state at frozen SHA `d0a4ed4ec`

- Dialect generators present for all 4 databases.
- `crates/fraiseql-server/src/tenancy/schema_isolation.rs` is PostgreSQL-specific (uses `SET search_path` + 63-char identifier cap).
- No SQL Server analog (`SCHEMA` per tenant + `EXEC sp_set_session_context`).
- No MySQL analog (`DATABASE` per tenant + `USE` per session).
- No published parity matrix.

## Target state

### Part 1 — parity audit

A published matrix in `/databases/compatibility` or a dedicated doc, with one row per feature × one column per DB. Cells: ✅ works, ⚠️ partial, ❌ not supported, with rationale + reproduction.

Features to audit:
- Subscriptions (WS + WAL when issue WAL-CDC ships).
- Row-Level Security primitives.
- Schema-isolation tenancy.
- Native aggregation columns.
- JSON operators (`->`, `->>`, `@>`).
- LTree hierarchies.
- Partial-period filters.
- Full-text search.
- Mutation `RETURNING`.

### Part 2 — multi-tenancy schema-isolation on MySQL + MSSQL

- **MySQL**: implement `database`-isolation mode. `CREATE DATABASE tenant_acme`; `USE tenant_acme` on connection acquisition. New helper `crates/fraiseql-server/src/tenancy/database_isolation.rs`.
- **MSSQL**: implement schema-per-tenant. `CREATE SCHEMA tenant_acme`; `EXEC sp_set_session_context N'tenant', N'acme'` per request. New helper `crates/fraiseql-server/src/tenancy/sqlserver_schema_isolation.rs`.
- Existing PostgreSQL `schema_isolation.rs` stays as the canonical pattern; new files mirror its surface.
- Add `[fraiseql.tenancy] mode = "schema"` validation: refuse to compile when the configured database doesn't support it (SQLite has no equivalent).

## Implementation sketch

1. Parity audit work first — at least one integration test per (feature, DB) cell, fail-loudly on the not-implemented ones.
2. MySQL and MSSQL schema-isolation helpers next, each behind a Cargo feature (`tenancy-isolation-mysql`, `tenancy-isolation-mssql`).
3. Compile-time validator extension: `[fraiseql.tenancy] mode` rejects unsupported combinations early rather than at runtime.

## Acceptance

- Published parity matrix in docs (renders in CI).
- MySQL database-isolation: end-to-end test creates two tenants, verifies cross-tenant data isolation, verifies hot-reload via ArcSwap.
- MSSQL schema-isolation: same end-to-end test.
- `SQLITE schema-isolation` returns a clear compile-time error.

items.title: SECURITY: cross-tenant RCE in multi-site mode via SQLite ATTACH — DB layer has no tenant isolation
items.body:
**Severity: Critical for multi-site deployments with untrusted/mutually-distrusting tenants. Verified by live exploitation on v0.6.3 (rev 3fbf68e).**

## Summary
In multi-site (`sites_dir`) mode the filesystem/shell sandbox holds, but the **database layer has zero tenant isolation**. The embedded SQLite engine runs inside the ephpm process, NOT under PHP's per-vhost `open_basedir`, so `ATTACH DATABASE` from any tenant's PHP is an arbitrary-filesystem read/write primitive — escalated to arbitrary code execution as another tenant.

## What holds (confirmed denied from a hostile vhost)
Per-vhost `open_basedir` (router.rs:1804 / vhost_open_basedir_value router.rs:2941), `disable_shell_exec` (main.rs:848), SQLite `load_extension` off, per-Host KV `Store` isolation (multi_tenant.rs) — absolute reads, `../` traversal, glob, exec family, cross-tenant KV all blocked.

## The hole (live-exploited, not inferred)
The SQLite DB is process-global: one `[db.sqlite].path` file, one wire listener shared by all vhosts; the MySQL proxy discards the handshake without validating creds (ephpm-db/src/mysql.rs:394-404); no SQL statement filtering on the tenant path (the ATTACH/PRAGMA allow-list at turso_cdc.rs:1341 covers only CDC replay). From a hostile `site-evil` vhost:
1. `mysqli_connect` with junk creds → connected; read site-a `wp_users.user_pass`.
2. `ATTACH DATABASE '.../site-b.db'` → read+wrote another tenant's DB.
3. `ATTACH DATABASE '.../sites/site-a/shell2.php'` → wrote a PHP file INTO another tenant's docroot (open_basedir bypass; PHP's own file_put_contents there was denied).
4. `GET /shell2.php` Host: site-a.localhost → executed the planted PHP as site-a. **Full cross-tenant RCE.**
5. Same ATTACH works through the always-on native `ephpm_db_execute()` bridge (db_bridge.rs) — firewalling the TCP proxy does NOT close it.

## Related
- HIGH (config-dependent): `sites_dir` + `[kv.redis_compat] enabled` + `[kv] secret` unset → RESP serves the global store unauthenticated (server.rs:328-336,383); startup only warn!s.
- MEDIUM: per-site DB isolation isn't expressible — `[db.sqlite].path` is one global file.
- LOW: PHP ETag cache key lacks a hostname component (router.rs:3039); KV store keyed on un-normalized Host (case-variant Hosts get separate stores).

## Fix directions
1. Reject `ATTACH` + filesystem-path `PRAGMA`/`VACUUM INTO` on BOTH the wire proxy and the native bridge (reuse the CDC allow-list pattern); open connections with SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DEFENSIVE + SQLITE_LIMIT_ATTACHED=0.
2. Physically separate tenants at the DB layer (per-vhost DB); if the proxy stays, validate per-site creds.
3. **PR-preview / untrusted code (post-0.7.0 bot): do NOT rely on in-process open_basedir + shared DB — each site needs its own process/container/namespace.**
4. Fail closed on the unauthenticated-KV config.

Found via authorized pen-test on the owner's own software; full repro retained.

items.title: Add Document Processing TypeORM persistence and runtime composition
items.body:
Parent Epic: #289
Depends on: #292

## Goal

- Implement the package-owned TypeORM persistence adapter and database schema for `DocumentProcessing`.
- Enforce tenant isolation and one-processing-per-tenant/document uniqueness at the database boundary.
- Expose the package `/typeorm` composition contracts and complete the framework-agnostic `/runtime` manifest so the package is hostable through the existing shared execution runtime.
- Add persistence/composition tests at the boundaries that own those guarantees.

## Instructions

- Follow root `AGENTS.md`, `packages/AGENTS.md` and `docs/engineering/package-guidelines.md`, especially the persistence, TypeORM, tenant-ownership and runtime-manifest rules.
- Use `packages/documents/src/lib/persistence/typeorm/`, `packages/documents/src/typeorm.ts` and `packages/documents/src/runtime.ts` as the closest proven responsibility references. Reuse their ownership boundaries without copying Documents-specific schema fields or uniqueness rules.
- Keep the hosting-service `DataSource` lifecycle outside this package. The package owns entities, migrations, mapper/repository adapter knowledge and its persistence factory; the future service will own the real `DataSource`.
- Tenant-owned lookups and mutations must enforce tenant scope in database predicates. Do not load globally and compare tenant afterward.
- Enforce tenant-local uniqueness for `(tenant_id, document_id)` in the database and translate expected duplicate/create-or-existing behavior into the package persistence contract rather than leaking database-specific errors to handlers.
- Keep state-transition and state-shape business invariants owned by the aggregate and restore/mapping boundary. Add database constraints only where current repository guidance or a concrete concurrency/data-integrity requirement makes the database the owning boundary; do not duplicate aggregate rules mechanically as schema policy.
- Keep EDP transaction propagation, execution log, Outbox and Runner composition in the existing shared runtime. Do not reproduce those mechanisms in the package.
- Create the task branch from the latest `epic-document-processing-package` branch and target the task PR back to `epic-document-processing-package`.

## Success criteria

- A package-owned TypeORM entity persists processing id, tenant id, source document id, status, extracted text and failure reason with persistence shapes that can round-trip every valid aggregate state.
- A package-owned migration creates the Document Processing schema required by this Epic.
- The database enforces uniqueness for `(tenant_id, document_id)`.
- Persistence create/reuse behavior is safe under the database uniqueness rule and returns the contract-level `created | existing` outcome expected by the prepare handler.
- Every lookup required by the persistence port includes tenant scope in its query predicate.
- Update includes tenant scope in the mutation boundary and does not permit cross-tenant mutation.
- Mapper/restore behavior preserves aggregate invariants and rejects persisted state that cannot restore to a valid aggregate rather than moving business rules into the persistence representation.
- `/typeorm` exposes the package entity/migration composition constants, persistence runtime token and factory without exposing concrete adapter internals through the root business entrypoint.
- `/runtime` uses the existing `defineRuntimePackage(...)` contract to aggregate the package execution bindings and TypeORM persistence contributions without duplicating handler or adapter construction knowledge.
- Persistence integration tests prove tenant isolation, tenant-local uniqueness/create-or-existing behavior, valid-state round-tripping and cross-tenant absence semantics.
- Composition tests prove the package execution/TypeORM runtime contributions are complete without introducing Nest imports into the business package.
- No service, HTTP presenter, event consumer, broker/CDC integration, ObjectStorage read or extractor implementation is introduced.
- Relevant Nx lint, typecheck, test and build checks for the package are green.

<details>
<summary>Previous issue body (verbatim)</summary>

## Current state

## Context

This is the control path for incremental snapshots, where an operator sends a command to one tenant's Debezium connector. SQL Server CDC records committed database changes in CDC tables. Debezium reads those records and publishes events to Kafka, while its signal consumer reads the control command; that signal consumer must not let one tenant advance another tenant's command bookmark.

## Why this matters

Separate topic and group state prevents a running tenant connector from skipping a command intended for a stopped tenant. The issue remains blocked until #141 releases the connector path it owns.

## Historical evidence

The text below is retained from the original issue as historical evidence and planning context. For open work, unchecked acceptance items and unmerged plans are not evidence of completion.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Short answer

Give every tenant's Debezium connector its own Kafka signal topic and its own
signal consumer group.

An operator writes a command such as `execute-snapshot` to the tenant's signal
topic. A Kafka consumer inside Debezium reads that command. The consumer-group
ID is the name of Debezium's bookmark in Kafka's `__consumer_offsets` internal
topic. The bookmark tells that connector which signal command to read next
after a restart.

The current configuration gives all tenant connectors one shared topic,
`connect-signals`, and does not set `signal.kafka.groupId`. Debezium therefore
uses its default group ID, `kafka-signal`, for every connector. The connectors
filter commands by Kafka message key, but they still share the same committed
bookmark. One connector can move that bookmark past a command that another,
stopped connector has not seen.

This ticket removes that shared state. A tenant's commands and signal bookmark
must be independent of every other tenant.

## Who uses the signal path

| Component | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Platform operator or operations script | Writes an `execute-snapshot`, `stop-snapshot`, `pause-snapshot`, or `resume-snapshot` command to the selected tenant's signal topic. |
| Debezium inside Kafka Connect | Runs one Kafka signal consumer for each tenant connector and acts only on messages whose key matches that connector's `topic.prefix`. |
| Kafka group coordinator | Stores each signal consumer's committed topic position under its `signal.kafka.groupId` in `__consumer_offsets`. |
| SQL Server signaling table | Stores the OPEN and CLOSE watermarks Debezium needs while an incremental snapshot is running. The Kafka signal starts the work; the SQL table controls snapshot-window deduplication. |
| Downstream application consumer | Does not read the signal topic. Its consumer group and output-topic offsets are unrelated to Debezium's signal consumer. |

The signal topic is a connector control path. It is not a way to reset or
resynchronize a new downstream Kafka consumer group. A downstream group replays
retained Kafka events by starting at the earliest retained offset or by having
its own offsets reset.

## Current failure example

```text
1. Tenant A's connector is stopped.
2. An operator writes a Tenant A snapshot command at offset 20 of connect-signals.
3. Tenant B's connector reads offset 20.
4. Tenant B ignores the command because the key belongs to Tenant A.
5. Tenant B commits the shared kafka-signal group position as offset 21.
6. Tenant A restarts from the shared position, offset 21.
7. Tenant A never reads its command at offset 20.
```

Debezium 3.6.1.Final creates a Kafka consumer for the signal channel, defaults
its group ID to `kafka-signal`, enables automatic offset commits, and skips a
record when its key does not match the connector's logical name. Those
behaviors are useful when each connector has a separate topic or bookmark. The
current combination of one shared topic and one shared bookmark is the defect.

References:

- [Debezium 3.6 SQL Server signal configuration](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/3.6/connectors/sqlserver.html)
- [Debezium 3.6 signaling channels](https://debezium.io/documentation/reference/3.6/configuration/signalling.html)
- [Debezium 3.6.1.Final Kafka signal consumer implementation](https://github.com/debezium/debezium/blob/v3.6.1.Final/debezium-connector-common/src/main/java/io/debezium/pipeline/signal/channels/KafkaSignalChannel.java)
- [Apache Kafka consumer offset tracking](https://kafka.apache.org/43/implementation/distribution/)

## Target design

The three build-scale tenants get these independent resources:

| Tenant | Signal topic | Debezium signal group | Required Kafka message key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lexfield-001` | `connect-signals-lexfield-001` | `kafka-signal-lexfield-001` | `tenant-lexfield-001` |
| `lexfield-002` | `connect-signals-lexfield-002` | `kafka-signal-lexfield-002` | `tenant-lexfield-002` |
| `lexfield-003` | `connect-signals-lexfield-003` | `kafka-signal-lexfield-003` | `tenant-lexfield-003` |

The three names have different jobs:

- `signal.kafka.topic` selects the Kafka topic that holds this tenant's commands.
- `signal.kafka.groupId` gives this connector an independent command bookmark.
- The Kafka message key remains the connector's `topic.prefix`; Debezium rejects a different key even when the command was written to the correct topic.

For example, the generated connector configuration for `lexfield-002` must
contain:

```json
{
  "topic.prefix": "tenant-lexfield-002",
  "signal.kafka.topic": "connect-signals-lexfield-002",
  "signal.kafka.groupId": "kafka-signal-lexfield-002"
}
```

The operator must write the command to `connect-signals-lexfield-002` with the
Kafka key `tenant-lexfield-002`.

## Behavior

When this ticket merges:

1. The connector generator derives a unique signal topic and signal group from
   every manifest tenant ID.
2. The disposable Kafka chart creates one single-partition signal topic for
   each of the three build-scale tenants and no shared `connect-signals` topic.
3. The Connect Kafka identity can read the `connect-signals-` topic prefix and
   the `kafka-signal-` group prefix.
4. The operations Kafka identity can write the `connect-signals-` topic prefix.
5. A signal queued while one tenant connector is stopped remains available to
   that connector even when another tenant processes its own signals.
6. Documentation tells a first-time operator how to select the topic and key,
   and how to distinguish the signal offset from the connector's SQL LSN in
   `connect-offsets`.

## Blocked by

- [x] #141
- [x] #172

Issue #141 owns `connect/connectors/` while it removes the obsolete custom SMT.
It must close before this ticket edits the connector template and golden files.

Issue #172 also edits `docs/specs/01-wire-format.md`, which this ticket declares,
in a disjoint region: #172 edits the event-envelope section near the top of the
file, while this ticket edits the signal-topic and offset text near the end. The
edge records that #172 merges first and this ticket then rebases its
wire-format edits onto the result, resolving any textual conflict at that point.
Added 2026-08-28 at Hari's direction (session s2); see the overlap note on #172.

## Paths

- `.github/workflows/gitops-kind.yml` (expected topic names only)
- `connect/connectors/connector-template.json`
- `connect/connectors/tests/connector-configs.golden`
- `connect/connectors/Lexfield.ConnectorGenerator.Tests/ConnectorGeneratorTests.cs`
- `connect/connectors/README.md`
- `infra/disposable/kafka/topics.yaml`
- `infra/disposable/kafka/users.yaml`
- `infra/disposable/kafka/README.md`
- `tests/Lexfield.Connect.Tests/Snapshots/IncrementalSnapshotFixture.cs`
- `tests/Lexfield.Connect.Tests/Snapshots/IncrementalSnapshotTests.cs`
- `docs/specs/01-wire-format.md` (signal topics and offset explanation only)
- `docs/specs/30-connect.md` (signal configuration and verification row only)

## Verification

Method: containers

Run the connector-generator tests:

```text
dotnet test connect/connectors/Lexfield.ConnectorGenerator.Tests/Lexfield.ConnectorGenerator.Tests.csproj
```

The golden output and focused assertions must prove that all three generated
connectors have different `signal.kafka.topic` and `signal.kafka.groupId`
values derived from their tenant IDs.

Run the incremental-snapshot container tests:

```text
dotnet test tests/Lexfield.Connect.Tests/Lexfield.Connect.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~Snapshots
```

The container test must run two tenant connectors. Stop Tenant A's connector,
write a command to Tenant A's topic, let Tenant B process a command from Tenant
B's topic, and then restart Tenant A. Tenant A must process its queued command.
Tenant B must not re-snapshot because of Tenant A's command.

The `gitops-kind` workflow must reconcile exactly three signal topics and must
verify the updated topic and group ACL declarations without Azure.

Run the repository ASCII and documentation checks over the changed docs.

## Acceptance checklist

- [ ] Every generated tenant connector has `signal.kafka.topic=connect-signals-{tenantId}`
- [ ] Every generated tenant connector has `signal.kafka.groupId=kafka-signal-{tenantId}`
- [ ] The signal Kafka message key remains exactly equal to `topic.prefix`
- [ ] The three build-scale signal topics exist with one partition each
- [ ] The shared `connect-signals` topic and literal `kafka-signal` group ACL are removed
- [ ] Connect has read access to the per-tenant signal topic and group prefixes
- [ ] Operations has write access to the per-tenant signal topic prefix
- [ ] Generator tests fail if two tenant configurations share a signal topic or signal group
- [ ] A two-tenant container test proves one connector cannot consume or skip another tenant's command
- [ ] A command written while Tenant A is stopped is processed after Tenant A restarts, even after Tenant B processes another command
- [ ] The existing incremental snapshot still re-emits the expected Outbox row through the normal transform chain
- [ ] Operator documentation gives the exact topic, message key, and JSON command for one concrete tenant
- [ ] Documentation separates the signal bookmark in `__consumer_offsets` from the Debezium SQL LSN and snapshot state in `connect-offsets`
- [ ] Documentation states that the signal topic does not reset a downstream consumer group
- [ ] No deploy-time generated connector file, tenant manifest, secret, connection string, or environment ID is committed

## Out of scope

- Changing the SQL Server `dbo.DebeziumSignal` watermark table or its grants
- Resetting or renaming downstream application consumer groups
- Changing `__consumer_offsets` directly
- Automating Kafka topic creation beyond the three build-scale tenants; fleet automation beyond n=3 is deferred from v1
- Migrating commands that are already pending on the old shared topic
- Changing Kafka authentication; #129 owns the separate Entra OAuth planning decision
- Running Terraform apply, Terraform destroy, or a live Azure test

## Size forecast

Implementation and verification PR: 10 files and at most 500 changed lines.

Contract documentation PR: 2 files and at most 180 changed lines. Open this PR
before the implementation PR merges, link both PRs, and keep both under this
ticket so the documented operator path lands with the behavior it describes.

---

Area: `connect/` and `infra/disposable` | Verification: containers | No `ready-for-agent` label requested.

items.title: Epic: Migrate Falcone document database from MongoDB to FerretDB v2 + DocumentDB
items.body:
# Epic: Migrate Falcone document database from MongoDB to FerretDB v2 + DocumentDB

## Problem
Falcone bundles **MongoDB** (`bitnami/mongodb:8.0.0`, single-node replica-set StatefulSet — `charts/in-falcone/values.yaml:1792-1874`) as its tenant-facing **document store** and as the change-event source for **realtime** and **CDC**. MongoDB is licensed under the **SSPL**, which the OSI does not recognize as open source and which is purpose-built to prohibit offering the software as a managed service/DBaaS without open-sourcing the entire surrounding stack. Falcone serves a document database to tenants over the network — exactly the prohibited use case, and a stricter restriction than AGPL. We must move to a permissively-licensed, genuinely open-source, MongoDB-compatible document store.

## Decision
Migrate to **FerretDB v2 (Apache-2.0)** backed by the **DocumentDB PostgreSQL extension (MIT)**. Rationale (recorded in **ADR-14**):
- **License fit:** Apache-2.0 + MIT — no SSPL/AGPL reciprocity for a BaaS.
- **No single-vendor rug-pull:** DocumentDB is Linux-Foundation-governed (vendor-neutral, PostgreSQL-first; AWS/Microsoft/Google participating).
- **Wire compatibility:** FerretDB speaks the MongoDB 5.0+ wire protocol; DocumentDB is the engine behind vCore Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB.
- **Leverages our PostgreSQL:** document workloads consolidate onto the Postgres engine and tenancy model Falcone already operates (schema-per-tenant + RLS, ADR-1).
- **AI-ready (opportunity, out of scope):** DocumentDB ships native DiskANN vector indexing.

Rejected: Percona Server for MongoDB (still SSPL); native Postgres JSONB (license-clean but not wire-compatible — would force tenant rewrites); ArangoDB (BSL), RavenDB (AGPL), Couchbase (source-available).

## What's actually in the code (grounding)
- **MongoDB is core, not peripheral:** tenant-facing document CRUD/query/aggregate (`apps/control-plane/src/runtime/mongo-data-executor.mjs`, plan builder `services/adapters/src/mongodb-data-api.mjs`), realtime SSE (`apps/control-plane/src/runtime/realtime-executor.mjs`, ADR-6), CDC->Kafka (`services/mongo-cdc-bridge/src/ChangeStreamWatcher.mjs`).
- **Tenants never touch MongoDB directly.** Single shared credential (`MONGO_URI`, `main.mjs::mongoUri`); isolation is app-level `tenantId` injection (`applyTenantScopeToFilter`/`injectTenantIntoDocument`, default field `tenantId`). **There is no tenant-facing Mongo wire endpoint to preserve** — only Falcone's internal connection changes.
- **Per-tenant Mongo credentials are advertised but unimplemented** (`scoped_credential` in the adapter spec; no executor/routes) — analogous to the SeaweedFS epic's synthetic credentials. This epic delivers the **first real per-tenant document-store identities**.
- **🚩 Change streams are used in TWO places** (`realtime-executor.mjs`, `mongo-cdc-bridge/ChangeStreamWatcher.mjs`) with `watch()`, `$match` on `fullDocument.tenantId`, `fullDocumentBeforeChange` pre-images, and resume tokens. **FerretDB v2 does not support change streams.** This is the dominant migration risk (child #F, P0).
- **🚩 Transactions** are declared in the adapter (`snapshot`/`majority`); **FerretDB v2 does not support multi-document transactions** (`commit`/`abortTransaction` unimplemented — FerretDB #1547/#1548).
- Replica set is mandatory today **only** because of change streams. No GridFS (object store is SeaweedFS). No server-side JS, no text/geo/wildcard indexes, no `$graphLookup`/`$unionWith`/`$out`/`$merge`.

## Design tenets
- **Tenant-facing API contract unchanged** (`/v1/collections/*`, realtime SSE, CDC topics). Migration is transparent to tenants.
- FerretDB + DocumentDB are **internal platform components**, never exposed to tenants.
- **Two-layer system:** stateless FerretDB gateway -> DocumentDB-on-Postgres engine. Internal-only backend networking.
- **Version-coupled, pinned pair**, documented upgrade order (engine before gateway).
- **Real per-tenant DocumentDB databases/roles** (replacing today's shared credential + unimplemented synthetic per-tenant keys), mapped onto Falcone's schema-per-tenant + RLS model.
- **Change streams must be re-sourced** off the new stack (Postgres logical replication / triggers) preserving tenant scoping and pre-image/delete semantics — see child #F. **This is the make-or-break item.**
- **Reversible:** MongoDB kept read-only as a fallback for a defined window.

## Pinned version pair (verified against FerretDB official docs)
- Gateway: `ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb:2.7.0`
- Engine: `ghcr.io/ferretdb/postgres-documentdb:17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0`
- `shared_preload_libraries = 'pg_cron,pg_documentdb_core,pg_documentdb'`; `cron.database_name='postgres'` + required `documentdb.*` GUCs.
- **Upgrade order:** install/upgrade the DocumentDB engine first, FerretDB second — never FerretDB ahead of a matching DocumentDB.

## Child issues
- [ ] #455 — ADR-14 + FerretDB/DocumentDB compatibility audit, tenancy-on-Postgres spike, version pinning (`add-ferretdb-adr-spike`)
- [ ] #456 — Deploy the DocumentDB engine: Postgres + DocumentDB extension on K8s/OpenShift (`add-ferretdb-documentdb-engine`)
- [ ] #457 — Deploy the FerretDB gateway: stateless wire endpoint, scaling, TLS, internal-only (`add-ferretdb-gateway`)
- [ ] #458 — Per-tenant isolation & credentials on real per-tenant DocumentDB databases/roles (`add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials`)
- [ ] #459 — Data-access cutover: point Falcone's Mongo client at FerretDB; compat shims (`add-ferretdb-data-access-cutover`)
- [ ] #460 — 🚩 Realtime + CDC change-stream remediation off the new stack (`add-ferretdb-realtime-cdc-remediation`)
- [ ] #461 — Data migration tooling + cutover runbook (mongodump/mongorestore initial + delta) (`add-ferretdb-data-migration-runbook`)
- [ ] #462 — Validation: data parity + per-tenant app-level smoke on the risk areas (`add-ferretdb-migration-validation`)
- [ ] #463 — Rollback plan: MongoDB read-only fallback window + procedure (`add-ferretdb-rollback-plan`)
- [ ] #464 — E2E: Playwright document CRUD/query/aggregation/auth/isolation + realtime on kind (`add-ferretdb-document-store-e2e`)
- [ ] #465 — Docs: two-layer architecture/runbook + licensing note + update MongoDB references (`add-ferretdb-document-store-docs`)

## Epic acceptance criteria (definition of done)
- [ ] ADR-14 merged; compatibility audit + tenancy spike recorded; version pair pinned with upgrade order.
- [ ] DocumentDB-on-Postgres + FerretDB deployable on kind and OpenShift, internal-only, SCC/non-root/fsGroup clean.
- [ ] Falcone's document store runs on FerretDB with the tenant-facing contract unchanged; contract/unit/adapter suites green.
- [ ] **Realtime + CDC re-sourced and tenant-scoped** on the new stack (or an explicitly accepted, documented degradation).
- [ ] **Real per-tenant DocumentDB databases/roles** provisioned/rotated/revoked; cross-tenant isolation probes pass.
- [ ] Scripted, verifiable data migration + cutover runbook exercised on a non-prod copy; parity checks pass.
- [ ] Document-store E2E suite green on kind. Rollback documented + tested. Docs/README MongoDB references updated.
- [ ] `bash tests/blackbox/run.sh` + CI `quality` job green throughout.

## Out of scope (epic)
- DiskANN/vector features beyond what already exists (the pgvector path stays as-is).
- Expanding the tenant-facing surface beyond what is wired today.
- Migrating any non-Falcone deployment overlays.

## OpenSpec changes
All 11 child changes are scaffolded under `openspec/changes/` and pass `openspec validate <id> --strict` ✅ (status: **proposed**, 0 tasks done — ready for `/opsx:apply`):
`add-ferretdb-adr-spike`, `add-ferretdb-documentdb-engine`, `add-ferretdb-gateway`, `add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials`, `add-ferretdb-data-access-cutover`, `add-ferretdb-realtime-cdc-remediation`, `add-ferretdb-data-migration-runbook`, `add-ferretdb-migration-validation`, `add-ferretdb-rollback-plan`, `add-ferretdb-document-store-e2e`, `add-ferretdb-document-store-docs`.

New capability specs introduced by this epic: `document-store-migration-validation` (via `add-ferretdb-migration-validation`) and `document-store-docs` (via `add-ferretdb-document-store-docs`).

items.title: FerretDB migration: ADR-14 + compatibility audit & tenancy-on-Postgres spike (version pinning)
items.body:
## Problem
The migration decision and its hard constraints must be recorded and de-risked before any deployment. Falcone's real MongoDB feature usage must be audited against the **current** FerretDB 2.7 / DocumentDB 0.107 matrix, and the per-tenant-on-Postgres mapping resolved with a spike. Two confirmed gaps gate the whole effort: **FerretDB v2 has no change streams** (Falcone uses them for realtime + CDC) and **no multi-document transactions** (`commit`/`abortTransaction` unimplemented).

## Proposed solution
- Write **ADR-14** in `docs-site/architecture/adrs.md` (decision, license rationale, LF governance, wire compatibility, Postgres leverage, AI-ready note, rejected alternatives: Percona/SSPL, JSONB/not-wire-compatible, ArangoDB/RavenDB/Couchbase).
- Produce a **compatibility matrix** of Falcone's actual usage (aggregation stages, index types, transactions, change streams) vs FerretDB 2.7 / DocumentDB 0.107, with a **remediation path per gap**.
- **Spike** the tenancy mechanics: how a FerretDB "database" resolves to an isolated backend given the decision to use **real per-tenant DocumentDB databases/roles** mapped onto Falcone's schema-per-tenant + RLS model. Resolve the exact database/role/auth mapping (the *choice* to go per-tenant is already made; the spike pins the *how*).
- Decide & record **colocated vs dedicated Postgres** for DocumentDB, factoring `shared_preload_libraries` and resource isolation.
- **Pin the version pair** (`ferretdb:2.7.0` <-> `postgres-documentdb:17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0`) and document the upgrade order (engine first, gateway second).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR-14 merged with rationale + rejected alternatives.
- [ ] Compatibility matrix committed; **change streams** and **multi-doc transactions** explicitly called out with remediation owners.
- [ ] `$lookup`/`$facet`/`$group`/TTL/unique index behavior verified against the live FerretDB/DocumentDB versions (not third-party blogs).
- [ ] Per-tenant DocumentDB database/role mapping mechanics recorded; colocated-vs-dedicated decision recorded.
- [ ] Pinned versions + upgrade order documented.

## Out of scope
- Any deployment or code change (downstream children).

## Dependencies
- None. **Gates every other child.**

**Epic:** #454



---

## OpenSpec change
- Package: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-adr-spike/` — validated `openspec validate add-ferretdb-adr-spike --strict` ✅
- Capability spec deltas: `data-api`
- Status: **proposed** (0/39 tasks). Implement with `/opsx:apply add-ferretdb-adr-spike` (features) or `/fix-bug add-ferretdb-adr-spike` (bugs); verify `/opsx:verify add-ferretdb-adr-spike`; archive `/opsx:archive add-ferretdb-adr-spike`.

items.title: Add support for MongoDB and SQL
items.body:
As we have with the C# version of Arc for supporting MongoDB and SQL / Relational databases, we need packages that are providing additional setup and help to work in the Cratis environment and provide productivity and support for things like multi tenancy and observable queries.

Like we have for the Cratis.Arc.MongoDB and Cratis.Arc.EntityFrameworkCore we want to add packages for Java / Kotlin that provide the same functionality we have there.

For MongoDB it should be built on top of Spring Data Mongo. 
For SQL / relational database it should be built on top of Spring Data JPA.

## Read Model naming

We have a way of deciding on naming schemes represented which is the `INamingPolicy` and then a `DefaultNamingPolicy`. We should have a similar thing implemented here and it should use the **Evo Inflector** library for handling the default pluralization. This will be compatible with how the Cratis Chronicle Kernel handles pluralization of read models when doing projections.

## Multi tenancy

In C# we have a transparent handling of multi tenancy built around different ways of setting this up, such as HTTP headers, sub domains and what not. We need to have the same core concept in the Arc Kotlin core, hooked up in a similar to access current tenant for the current call context - we use `AsyncLocal<>` in C# for what sits behind the tenant accessor, do what is correct for Kotlin & Java. 

We should hook up the IOC container so that we can take dependencies to the correct constructs like a mongo database or a mongocollection for a read model, in the same way we have done in Arc for C#. This should then resolve the tenancy and give you an instance of these things that are bound to the correct database based on that tenant. If no tenant is provided, it should have a fallback in the same way we do for C#.

## Observability

Based on observability leveraging reactive extensions (see issue #201), we want to provide additional convenience tooling for creating observable queries.

It should be in the same way as we have with C# with extension methods that extend a type, e.g. for MongoDB the Mongo collection type (interface). The methods we should support are the same as in C# with the different `.observe*` methods and support filtering which is the correct type for Mongo and JPA Spring Data providers.

Kotlin has extension functions which is similar to C#, so we would do that. But for Java we need to lean into a 3rd party library and Manifold seems to be the most unobtrusive with its `@Extension` annotation for the extension methods/functions. We don’t want to repeat the logic, so the Java specific extension and the Kotlin one should just call into a common static functionality for the actual implementations of the observe methods.

items.title: Migration validation: data-parity checks + per-tenant app-level smoke on the risk areas
items.body:
> Updated to reconcile with ADR-14 spike findings (PR #467). Source of truth: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-migration-validation/`.

## Problem

Raw data parity is not enough; the migration's concrete compatibility findings must be exercised
per tenant through Falcone's public API against the migrated stack before cutover is declared safe.
ADR-14 (merged, PR #467) surfaces the following definitive findings against
`ghcr.io/ferretdb/postgres-documentdb:17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0` / `ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb:2.7.0`:

- **Change streams unimplemented**: `collection.watch()` → CommandNotSupported (error 115);
  `changeStreamPreAndPostImages` → UnknownBsonField (error 40415). Realtime/CDC is broken; tracked
  in `add-ferretdb-realtime-cdc-remediation` (#460).
- **Multi-document transactions unimplemented** (deterministic failure): commit → CommandNotFound
  (error 59); **abort is a SILENT NO-OP — data written in an aborted transaction is NOT rolled
  back**. This is a data-integrity correctness hazard, not a degradation.
- **Cross-database `$lookup` rejected**: returns Location40321.
- **Same-namespace `$lookup` (≤1 join) and `$facet` (≤4 sub-pipelines): SUPPORTED** — these must
  return HTTP 200; a waiver path for these operators is not permitted because it would mask
  regressions. The ≤1/≤4 caps are enforced by the adapter allowlist in
  `services/adapters/src/mongodb-data-api.mjs`, not by FerretDB.
- **Isolation gap — no per-database role scoping**: a `tenant_a` credential can read `tenant_b`
  data at the DocumentDB backend level. The app-layer `tenantId` field filter in
  `services/adapters/src/mongodb-data-api.mjs` is the **sole enforced boundary**. Note:
  `apps/control-plane/src/postgres-applier.mjs` manages schemas/tables/views/extensions/grants only
  — it contains no Mongo role, createUser, or per-tenant DocumentDB identity provisioning logic.
- **Engine-first startup (pinned version pair)**: `postgres-documentdb:17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0`
  must be healthy before `ferretdb:2.7.0` starts; the runner must enforce this ordering.

Without automated checks wired into CI, the go/no-go decision for the MongoDB→FerretDB cutover
relies on manual inspection.

## Proposed solution

Automated data-parity checks plus per-tenant document-store-API smoke tests exercising each risk
area through Falcone's public interface:

- **Document-parity checker**: compares per-collection document counts and content checksums for
  two seeded tenants (A/B) between the migration manifest and the FerretDB/DocumentDB endpoint;
  exits non-zero on any unreviewed discrepancy.
- **Per-tenant API smoke** (tenants A and B) against the live routes
  `POST /v1/collections/{name}/documents`, `GET /v1/collections/{name}/documents`,
  `POST /v1/collections/{name}/query`, `GET /v1/collections/{name}/search` through
  `mongo-data-executor.mjs`, covering:
  - Aggregation `$lookup` (same-namespace, ≤1 join) — **SUPPORTED**, MUST return HTTP 200, no waiver.
  - Aggregation `$facet` (≤4 sub-pipelines) — **SUPPORTED**, MUST return HTTP 200, no waiver.
  - Aggregation `$group` — **SUPPORTED**, MUST return HTTP 200.
  - Cross-database `$lookup` — **REJECTED** (Location40321); probe asserts this exact code.
  - Unique / sparse / TTL / compound indexes — all **SUPPORTED**; no waiver.
  - Transaction commit → CommandNotFound (error 59) asserted with exact code; no "either succeeds"
    branch.
  - Transaction abort → silent no-op probe: write documents, call abort, read back and assert data
    is still present; recorded as ADR-14-referenced data-integrity finding.
  - CDC `watch()` probe → CommandNotSupported (error 115) asserted with exact code.
  - `changeStreamPreAndPostImages` probe → UnknownBsonField (error 40415) asserted with exact code.
- **Cross-tenant NEGATIVE probe**: Tenant A must receive HTTP 403 or HTTP 404 on Tenant B's resources.
- **Isolation-gap probe**: confirm backend read succeeds across tenant namespaces (no per-database
  role scoping enforced); record as ADR-14-referenced finding, not an unreviewed failure.
- **Engine-first startup enforcement**: runner starts and health-checks `postgres-documentdb` before
  `ferretdb`; both must be healthy before any test connects.
- Single entrypoint `tests/env/validation/run-ferretdb-validation.sh`; wired into
  `tests/blackbox/run.sh` behind `FERRETDB_VALIDATION=1` guard.

## Spec-delta (EARS)

Capability `document-store-migration-validation` — ADDED requirements:
- The system SHALL provide a document-parity checker comparing document counts and checksums per
  tenant against the migration manifest; exits non-zero on any unreviewed discrepancy.
- The system SHALL execute per-tenant smoke (tenants A/B) through the live document-store API;
  same-namespace `$lookup` and `$facet` MUST pass (HTTP 200, no waiver); cross-database `$lookup`
  MUST assert Location40321.
- The system SHALL assert transaction commit → CommandNotFound (error 59) and transaction abort →
  silent no-op with data NOT rolled back; both recorded as ADR-14 data-integrity findings.
- The system SHALL assert CDC `watch()` → error 115 and `changeStreamPreAndPostImages` → error
  40415 with exact error codes.
- The system SHALL execute an isolation-gap probe confirming per-database role scoping does NOT
  enforce cross-tenant denial; `postgres-applier.mjs` has no role/createUser/DocumentDB-identity
  logic.
- The system SHALL enforce engine-first startup: `postgres-documentdb:17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0`
  healthy before `ferretdb:2.7.0`; neither container connected until both healthy.
- The system SHALL deny Tenant A access to Tenant B's documents (HTTP 403 or 404).
- The system SHALL provide a single entrypoint exiting zero only on full pass or ADR-14-waived
  failures.

Capability `data-api` — ADDED requirements:
- The system SHALL return tenant-scoped results from document-store routes against both MongoDB
  and FerretDB/DocumentDB backends.
- The system SHALL deny cross-tenant document access (HTTP 403 or 404) at the route level.
- The system SHALL confirm supported aggregation operators return HTTP 200 without waiver; no
  waiver path exists for same-namespace `$lookup` or `$facet`.
- The system SHALL record the isolation gap (app-layer `tenantId` filter is sole boundary) with
  explicit ADR-14 reference.

Full spec deltas with scenarios (WHEN/THEN): `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-migration-validation/specs/document-store-migration-validation/spec.md` and `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-migration-validation/specs/data-api/spec.md`.

## Tasks

- [ ] **1. Prerequisites and fixture preparation** — resolve manifest format (OQ1), FerretDB port (OQ2); provision tenants A/B; capture checksum manifest; record ADR-14 error codes for tasks 3.5/3.6
- [ ] **2. Document-parity checker** (`tests/env/validation/ferretdb-parity-check.mjs`) — per-collection count + checksum comparison; structured JSON report; exception list; fallback live-diff mode; failing blackbox test before implementation
- [ ] **3. Per-tenant document-store-API smoke** (`tests/env/validation/ferretdb-smoke-data-api.mjs`):
  - 3.1–3.2 CRUD routes for tenants A and B; failing tests first
  - 3.3 Aggregation: same-namespace `$lookup` (HTTP 200, no waiver); `$facet` (HTTP 200, no waiver); `$group` (HTTP 200); cross-database `$lookup` (assert Location40321 exactly)
  - 3.4 Index smoke: unique (E11000), compound, sparse, TTL — all SUPPORTED, no waiver
  - 3.5 Transaction probes: commit → assert CommandNotFound error 59 exactly; abort → assert data NOT rolled back; both as ADR-14-referenced data-integrity findings
  - 3.6 CDC probes: `watch()` → assert error 115; `changeStreamPreAndPostImages` → assert error 40415; exact codes required
  - 3.7 Cross-tenant NEGATIVE probe (HTTP 403 or 404)
  - 3.8 Teardown hook (idempotent runs)
  - 3.9 Isolation-gap probe: backend read across tenant namespaces succeeds; confirm `postgres-applier.mjs` has no role/createUser logic; record as ADR-14 finding
- [ ] **3b. Engine-first startup** (`run-ferretdb-validation.sh`): start + health-check `postgres-documentdb:17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0`, then `ferretdb:2.7.0`; abort with named error on health-check failure
- [ ] **4. Single-entrypoint runner** (`tests/env/validation/run-ferretdb-validation.sh`) — sources `tests/env/env.sh`; runs parity then smoke; prints ADR-14 waiver summary; exits non-zero naming the failing check
- [ ] **5. CI integration** — `FERRETDB_VALIDATION=1` guard in `tests/blackbox/run.sh`; `quality` job step; `openspec validate add-ferretdb-migration-validation --strict` clean

Full task list: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-migration-validation/tasks.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Risk-area smoke green per ADR-14 findings:
  - Same-namespace `$lookup` (≤1 join) → HTTP 200, no waiver.
  - `$facet` (≤4 sub-pipelines) → HTTP 200, no waiver.
  - `$group` → HTTP 200.
  - Cross-database `$lookup` → Location40321 asserted exactly.
  - Unique / sparse / TTL / compound indexes → all pass, no waiver.
  - Transaction commit → CommandNotFound error 59 asserted exactly; no "either succeeds" branch.
  - Transaction abort → silent no-op confirmed; partial write detected and recorded as ADR-14 finding.
  - CDC `watch()` → error 115 asserted exactly.
  - `changeStreamPreAndPostImages` → error 40415 asserted exactly.
- [ ] Isolation-gap probe confirms backend-layer cross-tenant read succeeds; recorded as ADR-14 finding; `postgres-applier.mjs` confirmed to have no Mongo role/createUser/DocumentDB-identity logic.
- [ ] Cross-tenant NEGATIVE probe: Tenant A receives HTTP 403 or 404 on Tenant B's resources.

items.title: Per-tenant DocumentDB credentials + app-layer-authoritative isolation (wire-protocol createUser; RLS hardening; rotation/revocation)
items.body:
> Updated to reconcile with ADR-14 spike findings (PR #467). Source of truth: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials/`.

## Problem

Falcone's document-store isolation is **app-level only**: every tenant's collection reads, writes, and queries flow through a single shared Mongo credential resolved from `MONGO_URI` in `apps/control-plane/src/runtime/main.mjs::mongoUri` (lines 33-42). The per-tenant credential surface (`scoped_credential` / `MONGO_DATA_SCOPED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES`) is advertised in `services/adapters/src/mongodb-data-api.mjs` (lines 136, 138) and routed in `apps/control-plane/src/mongo-data-api.mjs` (lines 73-81) but has no backend implementation.

ADR-14 (spike `add-ferretdb-adr-spike`, merged) established the key tenancy facts for FerretDB 2.7.0 / postgres-documentdb 17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0:

- A Mongo "database" in DocumentDB is a **logical namespace** (a `database_name` value in the shared `documentdb_data` schema) — it is **not** a Postgres-database-per-tenant.
- The spike **disproved** per-database role scoping at the DocumentDB layer: a user created with `readWrite` on `tenant_a` successfully read `tenant_b`. DB-level credential isolation is **not** enforced at this engine version.
- `db.runCommand({createUser, roles:[...]})` over the MongoDB wire protocol provisions a real Postgres login role (LOGIN, non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS).
- App-layer `tenantId` injection (`applyTenantScopeToFilter` / `injectTenantIntoDocument` in `services/adapters/src/mongodb-data-api.mjs:620,655`) is the **authoritative** isolation boundary — unchanged by the engine swap.

This change delivers per-tenant DocumentDB credentials for **least-privilege auth and audit trail** (not as an isolation boundary), plus defense-in-depth RLS hardening documentation and the record of the hard-isolation architectural path.

## Proposed solution

Introduce a net-new DocumentDB identity applier (`services/provisioning-orchestrator/src/appliers/documentdb-identity-applier.mjs`) that provisions, rotates, and revokes per-tenant DocumentDB credentials via the MongoDB wire-protocol `createUser` / `updateUser` / `dropUser` commands. This applier is **net-new** — `postgres-applier.mjs` manages only `['schemas','tables','views','extensions','grants']` and has no role or identity logic.

- **App-layer `tenantId` scoping (`applyTenantScopeToFilter` / `injectTenantIntoDocument`) remains the authoritative isolation boundary** throughout. Per-tenant credentials provide least-privilege auth and audit, not cross-tenant denial at the backend layer.
- **Defense-in-depth**: optional RLS hardening (`ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + non-BYPASSRLS `falcone_app` role + `app.tenant_id` GUC on `documentdb_data` tables) is documented as a hardening layer, proven compatible with the DocumentDB engine in the spike.
- **Hard DB-level isolation** (credential-level cross-tenant denial) requires a dedicated Postgres database or instance per high-isolation tenant tier — documented as a future architecture option, explicitly out of scope for this change.
- Credential storage is consistent with Vault/ESO (ADR-9). No plaintext credentials persisted. Provisioning is issued at runtime over the MongoDB wire protocol.

OpenSpec change package: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials/`

## Spec delta (EARS — ADDED Requirements)

**Capability: `data-api`**

- **Tenant onboarding provisions a per-tenant DocumentDB credential via wire-protocol createUser** — The system SHALL issue `db.runCommand({createUser: 'falcone_doc_{tenantId}', roles:[{role:'readWrite', db:'falcone_doc_{tenantId}'}]})` over the MongoDB wire protocol, yielding a real Postgres login role (non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS). `⚠ not code-verifiable`: GUC names `documentdb.enableUserCrud` / `documentdb.maxUserLimit` — must be verified before implementation.
- **Per-tenant DocumentDB credential rotation is implemented and does not orphan access** — The system SHALL implement `updateUser` rotation, Vault/ESO update, `credential_rotation` audit event, and immediate old-password invalidation.
- **App-layer tenantId scoping is retained as the authoritative isolation layer for all data-api operations** — The system SHALL retain `applyTenantScopeToFilter` and `injectTenantIntoDocument` active on every document-store read and write.
- **Tenant->namespace/collection mapping is preserved at parity with the pre-migration MongoDB model** — The system SHALL map each tenant's collections to `falcone_doc_{tenantId}` using the same collection names.
- **Tenant offboarding revokes the per-tenant DocumentDB credential with no orphaned access** — The system SHALL issue `dropUser` and clean up the tenant's collections before marking deletion complete.

**Capability: `tenant-isolation`**

- **App-layer tenantId scoping is the authoritative document-store isolation boundary** — The system SHALL ensure `applyTenantScopeToFilter` and `injectTenantIntoDocument` are applied on every document-store read and write, regardless of credential or namespace.
- **Per-tenant DocumentDB credentials reduce blast radius and enable per-tenant audit** — The system SHALL provision a dedicated DocumentDB credential (non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS Postgres login role) per tenant; this credential does NOT substitute for app-layer isolation.
- **Optional RLS hardening on documentdb_data tables provides defense-in-depth** — The system SHALL support optional activation of `ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with non-BYPASSRLS role and `app.tenant_id` GUC (operator decision; consistent with `withTenantRlsContext`).
- **Hard DB-level isolation requires a dedicated Postgres instance per high-isolation tier** — The system SHALL document that a Mongo logical namespace does NOT enforce cross-tenant credential denial at this engine version; a dedicated Postgres database/instance per tier is the only architectural path to hard isolation.

## Tasks

- [ ] 1.1 Verify `add-ferretdb-adr-spike` merged and ADR-14 findings recorded (wire-protocol createUser/dropUser/updateUser command signatures confirmed)
- [ ] 1.2 Verify `add-ferretdb-documentdb-engine` merged and DocumentDB instance reachable in `tests/env/`
- [ ] 1.3 Verify `add-ferretdb-gateway` merged and FerretDB gateway can authenticate wire-protocol connections
- [ ] 1.4 Verify GUC names `documentdb.enableUserCrud` / `documentdb.maxUserLimit` against live engine (`⚠ not code-verifiable` at spec revision)
- [ ] 1.5 Confirm Vault/ESO secret path convention for per-tenant DocumentDB credentials (consistent with ADR-9)
- [ ] 2.1 Create net-new `services/provisioning-orchestrator/src/appliers/documentdb-identity-applier.mjs` with `provisionTenantIdentity`, `rotateTenantIdentityCredential`, `revokeTenantIdentity` — via wire-protocol only (NOT Postgres DDL; NOT `postgres-applier.mjs` extension)
- [ ] 2.2 Add idempotency check (`usersInfo` probe before `createUser`)
- [ ] 2.3 Add fail-closed guard: provisioning failure throws `DOCUMENTDB_IDENTITY_PROVISION_FAILED`; never falls through to shared `MONGO_URI`
- [ ] 2.4 Document in module header that credentials serve least-privilege auth/audit; app-layer scoping is authoritative
- [ ] 2.5 Unit tests for `documentdb-identity-applier.mjs` (mock wire-protocol client; provision/idempotent/fail-closed/rotation/revocation)
- [ ] 3.1 Implement credential generation and Vault/ESO write in `provisionTenantIdentity`
- [ ] 3.2 Implement `rotateTenantIdentityCredential` with `updateUser`, Vault/ESO update, `credential_rotation` audit event
- [ ] 3.3 Ensure test fixtures use non-provider credential literals (avoid GitHub push-protection rejections)
- [ ] 4.1 Wire `provisionTenantIdentity` into tenant onboarding lifecycle; fail onboarding on DocumentDB identity failure
- [ ] 4.2 Wire `revokeTenantIdentity` into tenant offboarding; confirm Postgres login role gone before deletion complete
- [ ] 4.3 Handle no-op offboarding for pre-migration tenants without existing DocumentDB credential
- [ ] 5.1 Update `apps/control-plane/src/runtime/main.mjs` to resolve per-tenant credentials via `secretRef`; retain shared `MONGO_URI` as fallback for back-fill window only
- [ ] 5.2 Confirm `applyTenantScopeToFilter` and `injectTenantIntoDocument` remain active on all data-api paths after credential resolver change; add dual-isolation integration assertion
- [ ] 6.1 Write back-fill script `scripts/backfill-ferretdb-tenant-identities.mjs` for existing tenants lacking DocumentDB credential
- [ ] 6.2 Add `--force-rotate` flag (default: no-force-rotate; resolves Design OQ1)
- [ ] 7.1-7.5 Blackbox tests: provision/idempotency, rotation, offboarding/revocation, two-tenant app-layer isolation probe, dual-isolation invariant
- [ ] 7.6 Do NOT write a test asserting DB-level credential denial — ADR-14 disproved this; such a test would be incorrect
- [ ] 8.1-8.3 Real-stack slice in `tests/env/`: full provision/rotate/revoke lifecycle; confirm no plaintext in relational record; confirm fail-closed on provisioning failure
- [ ] 9.1 Document optional RLS hardening steps (operator runbook, not committed as doc file)
- [ ] 10.1-10.3 Validation: `openspec validate --strict`; `bash tests/blackbox/run.sh`; real-stack `tests/env/` slice

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-tenant DocumentDB credential (non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS Postgres login role) provisioned on tenant onboarding via wire-protocol `createUser`; `DOCUMENTDB_IDENTITY_PROVISION_FAILED` thrown on failure — tenant never activated with shared `MONGO_URI`.
- [ ] Credential rotation implemented (`updateUser`) and tested; old credential invalidated immediately.
- [ ] Offboarding issues `dropUser`; Postgres login role confirmed gone before deletion complete; no-op for pre-migration tenants.
- [ ] `applyTenantScopeToFilter` / `injectTenantIntoDocument` retained active on every data-api code path; dual-isolation test confirms both layers simultaneously active.
- [ ] No test asserts DB-level credential denial at the engine layer (spike proved this does not hold).
- [ ] `tenant-isolation` / RLS contract suites green; no regressions in existing `data-api` suites.
- [ ] Optional RLS hardening documented as defense-in-depth layer; hard DB-level isolation documented as requiring a dedicated Postgres instance per tier.

## Out of scope

- Realtime/CDC tenant scoping (covered by `add-ferretdb-realtime-cdc-remediation`).
- Hard DB-level isolation (dedicated Postgres instance per tier) — documented as future option only.

## Dependencies

- `add-ferretdb-adr-spike` (#455), `add-ferretdb-documentdb-engine` (#456), `add-ferretdb-gateway` (#457).

**Epic:** #454
**Siblings:** #455 (ADR/spike), #456 (engine), #457 (gateway), #459 (data-access cutover), #460 (migration validation), #461 (rollback plan), #462 (runbook), #463 (CDC remediation), #464 (document-store docs), #465 (E2E)

---

## OpenSpec change

- Package: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials/` — validated `openspec validate add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials --strict` ✅
- Capability spec deltas: `data-api`, `tenant-isolation`
- Status: **proposed**. Implement with `/opsx:apply add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials`; verify `/opsx:verify add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials`; run `bash tests/blackbox/run.sh`; archive `/opsx:archive add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials`. Optional real E2E: `/e2e-issue add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials`.

items.title: smrt-web: change-feed spine — _smrt_changes log, tombstones, cursor API + generated _changes route
items.body:
## Parent

#1755

## What to build

The adapter-agnostic change-observation spine: an append-only `_smrt_changes` system table written by the framework's existing write-observation layer (the same interceptor mechanism reports and tenancy already use), exposed through one read interface and one generated route.

Every framework save/delete appends a change entry — monotonic per-database sequence, table, row id, operation, tenant, timestamp — with deletes recorded as tombstones. A single read interface returns changes since a cursor, filterable by table and tenant, and serves three eventual consumers: client delta pull, the SSE push channel, and the per-table version source for ETags. A generated, auth-guarded route exposes it over HTTP for web and mobile clients alike.

Must work identically on SQLite, Postgres, and DuckDB (it sits above the adapter — this is the design reason it exists instead of WAL-based CDC). Includes a retention/compaction policy so the log's growth is bounded, and a manual bump escape hatch for the documented gap: raw-SQL writes that bypass framework mutation paths are invisible to the feed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every framework save/delete appends exactly one change entry; deletes are tombstones distinguishable from updates
- [ ] The cursor is strictly monotonic per database; reads since a cursor miss no committed changes under concurrent writers (overlap-safe semantics documented and tested)
- [ ] Tenant-scoped reads never return another tenant's changes
- [ ] The generated changes route requires authentication, respects tenant context, and is documented as part of the client/mobile sync contract
- [ ] Retention/compaction keeps the log bounded; a manual bump API exists for out-of-band writers
- [ ] Test suite on real in-memory SQLite: cursor monotonicity, tombstones, tenant isolation, retention (prior art: the collection-cache and interceptor suites)

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately

items.title: Implement Process Document UseCase
items.body:
Parent Epic: #313
Depends on: #316, #318, #320, #322

## Goal

Implement the service-owned `ProcessDocumentUseCase` in `apps/services/document-processing` so it satisfies `specs/document-processing/process-document.md` cases `DPROC-PROC-001..005` using the already-hosted Document Processing Operations/Read plus the composed `ObjectStorage` and `DocumentExtractor` capabilities.

This task is the application orchestration only. It does not add transport, consumers, or new package behavior.

## Preflight findings

- EDP `@event-driven-platform/use-case-executor@0.1.0` claims one durable logical UseCase execution by the parent Intent, returns a stored completed result on replay, and on a thrown UseCase error calls `UseCaseExecutionStore.release(...)` before rethrowing the original error. It has no internal retry loop.
- EDP Runner derives execution identity from each child Operation Intent. A completed child execution is replayed from the execution log instead of running its handler again. Therefore the same logical Process Document execution may safely derive stable Prepare/Finish child Intent slots from the parent UseCase Intent.
- This replay is important for recovery: after Prepare returned `created`, a later retry of the same logical UseCase receives that stored `created` result rather than reclassifying its own durable `PENDING` record as an unrelated existing processing.
- A separate concurrent Process Document invocation has a different parent/child Intent. `PrepareDocumentProcessingHandler` delegates to `DocumentProcessingPersistence.createOrGetExisting(...)`; TypeORM uses insert-or-ignore plus tenant/document lookup, with database uniqueness owning one processing per `(tenant_id, document_id)`.
- `PrepareDocumentProcessingOperation` returns `created | existing` plus only `{ id, documentId, status }`. It does not return extracted text/failure reason.
- Therefore whenever Prepare returns `existing`, Process Document must execute the tenant-aware `GetDocumentProcessingRead` and decide from the current durable state rather than trusting the possibly stale status captured by the earlier Prepare result. This also lets a retry of a competing invocation observe a later `COMPLETED`/`FAILED` state.
- `GetDocumentProcessingReadHandler` already performs tenant-scoped lookup at persistence and returns the current `PENDING | COMPLETED | FAILED` state including terminal result data.
- `FinishDocumentProcessingHandler` owns the `PENDING -> COMPLETED/FAILED` transition through tenant-scoped persistence. Its update predicate requires the same tenant/id and current `PENDING`; successful completion also emits the package-owned completion event through Runner/Outbox.
- `ObjectStorage.get({ reference })` is the reusable opaque-reference read boundary. The UseCase must pass the supplied `storageReference` as-is and must not reconstruct a physical/logical storage key.
- `DocumentExtractor.extract(bytes)` owns representation detection and OCR selection. Its package-owned `DocumentExtractionError` is the current stable known extraction-failure surface (`unsupported-content` and `extraction-failed`); raw third-party OCR failures are normalized to that boundary.
- EDP `ExecutionFailureError` is the canonical classified execution error. `document-processing-in-progress` must use it with `retryable: true`; unknown errors must not be globally reclassified by this UseCase.

## Instructions

- Follow root `AGENTS.md`, `apps/services/AGENTS.md`, `docs/engineering/service-guidelines.md`, `packages/runtime-executions/AGENTS.md`, `docs/review/README.md`, and the accepted Process Document product spec.
- Use `RegisterDocumentUseCase` as the closest reference for stable derived child Intent slots, Runner execution, explicit actor/tenant propagation, and service-level external capability orchestration. Reuse the pattern only where the responsibilities match.
- Add `ProcessDocumentUseCase` in its own `application/use-cases/process-document/` folder with a concrete context extending EDP `UseCaseContext` and carrying actor + tenant.
- Input is exactly the application data required by the accepted spec: `documentId` and opaque `storageReference`; tenant remains context metadata.
- Give the UseCase a stable semantic name based on `documentProcessingName`.
- For a new processing, create the Prepare Operation, then read source bytes by opaque reference, extract text, and Finish `COMPLETED`.
- Treat a package-owned `DocumentExtractionError` as the current terminal extraction failure boundary: Finish `FAILED` with a durable failure reason derived from the package error and return the failed processing state.
- Let ObjectStorage errors and unknown/unclassified extractor errors propagate unchanged so the current logical UseCase execution is released by `UseCaseExecutor`; do not write a terminal outcome when failure semantics are not known by the application boundary.
- When Prepare returns `existing`, execute `GetDocumentProcessingRead` for the current tenant/document. Return stored `COMPLETED` or `FAILED` state directly. For current `PENDING`, throw `ExecutionFailureError` with code `document-processing-in-progress` and `retryable: true`.
- If Prepare reports `existing` but the owning Read unexpectedly returns `null`, fail rather than inventing a state or starting extraction.
- Register/export the UseCase through the existing `ApplicationModule`.
- Add specification-level tests traceable to `DPROC-PROC-001..005`. Tests may verify the observable requirement that existing terminal/PENDING paths do not load/extract/finish again, but must not reproduce EDP Runner/UseCaseExecutor replay, claim, retry-loop, transaction, or Outbox tests.
- Add only direct external package dependencies actually imported by the service (`@event-driven-platform/intent` and `@event-driven-platform/execution`) and keep lockfile/project references consistent.

## Do not

- Do not add a UseCase-local retry or polling loop. `UseCaseExecutor` owns claim/release/replay of the logical UseCase execution; the external invocation boundary owns whether/when a retry occurs.
- Do not add a recovery Read for a Prepare result that was `created`. Runner's deterministic child Intent replay already preserves the completed Prepare result for the same logical UseCase execution.
- Do not use the status embedded in an `existing` Prepare result as the authoritative current state. `GetDocumentProcessingReadHandler` + tenant-scoped persistence own the current-state read.
- Do not add local idempotency/deduplication/concurrency locks. `PrepareDocumentProcessingHandler`, TypeORM `createOrGetExisting`, and the `(tenant_id, document_id)` database uniqueness own tenant-local processing deduplication; EDP Runner/UseCaseExecutor own execution idempotency.
- Do not call package persistence or handlers directly. Use the shared `Runner`/`Reader` identities hosted by `RuntimeExecutionsModule`.
- Do not add service-local Runner, Reader, UseCaseExecutor, resolver, transaction, execution-log, Outbox, or retry wrappers/policies. `@accounterbro/runtime-executions` and EDP own those mechanisms.
- Do not reimplement the `PENDING -> terminal` invariant or completion event emission. `FinishDocumentProcessingHandler` / aggregate / persistence own those behaviors.
- Do not reconstruct `documents/<tenant>/<document>/original`, parse storage references, or import `LocalFolderStorage` in application code. `ObjectStorage.get` owns reference resolution.
- Do not inspect JPEG/Tesseract/language/model details or catch raw OCR-library errors. `DocumentExtractor` owns detection, technology selection, and normalization.
- Do not convert unknown ObjectStorage/extractor errors into `FAILED` or mark them retryable without a concrete owning classification contract.
- Do not add presenters, HTTP routes, event consumers, broker/CDC behavior, manual retry UseCases, S3, caching, or broader extracted-data models.
- Do not change `@accounterbro/document-processing`, `@accounterbro/object-storage`, or `@accounterbro/document-extraction` in this task unless verification exposes a concrete compatibility defect that is separately justified.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ProcessDocumentUseCase` is a singleton Nest injectable with a stable semantic name and concrete actor/tenant UseCase context.
- [ ] input contains `documentId + storageReference`; tenant is passed through context to every tenant-owned Operation/Read.
- [ ] `DPROC-PROC-001`: new processing executes Prepare -> ObjectStorage read -> DocumentExtractor -> Finish completed and returns `{ id, documentId, status: COMPLETED, extractedText }`.
- [ ] `DPROC-PROC-002`: package-owned terminal `DocumentExtractionError` executes Finish failed and returns `{ id, documentId, status: FAILED, failureReason }`; no extracted text is returned.
- [ ] unknown/unclassified storage/extraction failures propagate without Finish so durable processing remains `PENDING` for platform-level recovery of the same logical execution.
- [ ] `DPROC-PROC-003`: existing completed processing is re-read through `GetDocumentProcessingRead` and returned without storage read, extraction, or Finish.
- [ ] `DPROC-PROC-004`: existing failed processing is re-read and returned without storage read, extraction, automatic retry, or Finish.
- [ ] `DPROC-PROC-005`: existing current `PENDING` state throws canonical `ExecutionFailureError` with code `document-processing-in-progress` and `retryable: true`, without storage read/extraction/Finish or a local wait/retry loop.
- [ ] an inconsistent `existing + Read null` state does not start extraction or invent a processing result.
- [ ] application code uses only public `Runner`, `Reader`, `ObjectStorage`, `DocumentExtractor`, and Document Processing contracts; no package handlers/persistence/concrete infrastructure are imported.
- [ ] `ApplicationModule` provides/exports both Process Document and Get Document Processing UseCases.
- [ ] service dependencies/lockfile remain consistent and relevant Nx lint, typecheck, test and build are green.
- [ ] exact-head PR CI and current-head independent Codex review are clean before merge into `epic-313-document-processing-usecases`.

## Verification

Use the current Nx project identity `@accounterbro/document-processing-service` and run its smallest applicable lint, typecheck, test and build targets, plus `pnpm nx sync:check` if dependency/project-reference changes require it. Then require exact-head GitHub CI and an independent review for that exact head before merge.
