items.title: Docs: two-layer architecture/runbook + licensing note + update MongoDB references
items.body:
> Updated to reconcile with ADR-14 spike findings (PR #467). Source of truth: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-document-store-docs/`.

## Problem

After the MongoDB-to-FerretDB+DocumentDB migration (epic #454), internal documentation still references MongoDB as the document store and no authoritative two-layer architecture or operations runbook exists. Specifically:

- The earlier issue body described isolation as "one DocumentDB database + one role per tenant = isolation". **This is incorrect.** The verified model (ADR-14 spike) is: a Mongo "database" is a logical namespace in **one shared backing Postgres DB**; app-layer `tenantId` scoping (`applyTenantScopeToFilter` / `injectTenantIntoDocument` in `mongodb-data-api.mjs`) is the **authoritative isolation boundary**; RLS coexists as hardening; a per-tenant DocumentDB role does NOT provide isolation (a `tenant_a` role can read `tenant_b` data); hard isolation requires a **dedicated DocumentDB instance per tenant tier**.
- The aggregation compatibility row was incomplete: all 15 adapter-allowed aggregation stages are supported by the engine; `$out`/`$merge` are engine-functional but blocked by the Falcone adapter allowlist (policy decision, not engine limitation); `$lookup`/`$facet` are supported within the same database.
- The deployment topology was not documented: the DocumentDB engine requires a dedicated Postgres instance (colocated topology rejected due to image / `shared_preload_libraries` coupling); engine-first startup is required; bundled extensions are pgvector 0.8.1, PostGIS 3.6.0, rum 1.3, pg_cron 1.6.
- The change-streams row must name the pgoutput/logical-replication remediation direction and cross-reference `add-ferretdb-realtime-cdc-remediation` (#460).
- The transactions row must recommend idempotent single-document writes (not suggest multi-doc transactions will be supported).

Operators lack the topology, version-pinning constraints, upgrade-order rules, verified tenancy model, change-stream remediation guidance, and compatibility-differences table needed to run the new backend safely in production.

## Proposed solution

Author an authoritative FerretDB+DocumentDB architecture and operations runbook under `docs-site/architecture/ferretdb.md` covering:

- **Two-layer design**: FerretDB gateway (`ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb:2.7.0`) fronting DocumentDB engine (`ghcr.io/ferretdb/postgres-documentdb:17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0`)
- **Deployment topology**: dedicated Postgres instance; colocated topology rejected (image / `shared_preload_libraries` coupling); engine-first startup; bundled extensions pgvector 0.8.1, PostGIS 3.6.0, rum 1.3, pg_cron 1.6
- **Version pinning + upgrade order**: engine MUST be upgraded before gateway; gateway MUST NEVER advance ahead of a matching engine release; compatibility verified via engine image tag suffix (`ferretdb-2.7.0`)
- **PostgreSQL extension prerequisites**: `shared_preload_libraries='pg_cron,pg_documentdb_core,pg_documentdb'`; `cron.database_name='postgres'`; DocumentDB GUCs
- **Verified tenancy model**: shared backing Postgres DB; app-layer `tenantId` scoping (`applyTenantScopeToFilter` / `injectTenantIntoDocument`) authoritative; RLS as hardening; per-tenant role does NOT isolate; hard isolation only via dedicated DocumentDB instance per tier
- **Compatibility-differences + remediations table**: no change streams (pgoutput/logical-replication remediation, cross-ref `add-ferretdb-realtime-cdc-remediation` / #460); no multi-doc transactions (idempotent single-doc writes recommended); aggregation policy (`$out`/`$merge` blocked by adapter allowlist; all 15 adapter-allowed stages engine-supported; `$lookup`/`$facet` supported within same DB)
- **Licensing decision**: FerretDB (Apache-2.0) + DocumentDB extension (MIT) selected; MongoDB SSPL eliminated; cross-link ADR-14

Update stale MongoDB references in `docs-site/` and `README*` to FerretDB+DocumentDB equivalents.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Architecture/runbook doc merged at canonical path under `docs-site/architecture/`; all required sections present (two-layer design, deployment topology + bundled extensions, pinned pair + upgrade order, PostgreSQL prerequisites, verified tenancy model, compatibility-differences table, change-stream cross-reference to #460, observability, licensing).
- [ ] Tenancy model section states: shared backing Postgres DB; app-layer `tenantId` scoping authoritative; RLS as hardening; per-tenant role does NOT provide isolation; hard isolation requires dedicated DocumentDB instance per tier.
- [ ] Compatibility-differences table: change streams row names pgoutput/logical-replication as remediation direction and cross-references `add-ferretdb-realtime-cdc-remediation`; transactions row recommends idempotent single-doc writes; aggregation row correctly states all 15 adapter-allowed stages supported, `$out`/`$merge` blocked by adapter policy.
- [ ] Topology section: dedicated Postgres stated; colocated rejection recorded; engine-first startup explicit; bundled extensions listed (pgvector 0.8.1, PostGIS 3.6.0, rum 1.3, pg_cron 1.6).
- [ ] ADR-14 cross-linked bidirectionally (runbook to ADR-14; ADR-14 entry to runbook).
- [ ] Licensing note names MongoDB SSPL as eliminated alternative; links to ADR-14.
- [ ] No remaining docs/README occurrence presents MongoDB as the active document store.

## Out of scope

- ADR-14 itself (ADR/spike child, owned by `add-ferretdb-adr-spike`).
- Source code, Helm charts, tests, or API contracts.

## Dependencies

- `add-ferretdb-adr-spike` (ADR-14)
- `add-ferretdb-documentdb-engine` (engine topology / extension prerequisites)
- `add-ferretdb-gateway` (gateway config)
- `add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials` (per-tenant credential provisioning)
- `add-ferretdb-realtime-cdc-remediation` (#460; cross-ref for change-stream remediation section)

**Epic:** #454
**Siblings:** #460 (realtime-cdc-remediation), #461 (gateway), #462 (engine), #463 (data-access-cutover), #464 (e2e)

---

## OpenSpec change

- Change ID: `add-ferretdb-document-store-docs`
- Package: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-document-store-docs/`
- Capability spec deltas: `data-api`, `document-store-docs`
- Type: documentation | Priority: P2
- Status: **proposed** (0/30 tasks). Implement with `/opsx:apply add-ferretdb-document-store-docs`; verify `/opsx:verify add-ferretdb-document-store-docs`; archive `/opsx:archive add-ferretdb-document-store-docs`.

### Spec delta (EARS) — ADDED Requirements (`openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-document-store-docs/specs/`)

**`data-api` — Authoritative architecture documentation exists for the FerretDB+DocumentDB backend**
The system SHALL maintain an authoritative architecture and operations runbook for its active document-store backend (FerretDB+DocumentDB) covering: two-layer component topology; verified tenancy model (shared backing Postgres DB, app-layer `tenantId` scoping authoritative, RLS as hardening, hard isolation via dedicated DocumentDB instance per tier); version-pinning constraints; upgrade order; and known compatibility differences. No documentation file SHALL misidentify the active document-store backend.

**`document-store-docs` — FerretDB+DocumentDB architecture and operations runbook exists**
The system SHALL maintain a runbook at `docs-site/architecture/` describing the two-layer design, deployment topology (dedicated Postgres, colocated rejected, engine-first startup, bundled extensions pgvector 0.8.1 / PostGIS 3.6.0 / rum 1.3 / pg_cron 1.6), pinned image pair, upgrade order rule, PostgreSQL extension prerequisites, verified tenancy model, compatibility-differences table, and change-stream remediation cross-reference.

**`document-store-docs` — Pinned image pair documented with version-compatibility rationale**
The system SHALL document both pinned tags (`ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb:2.7.0` + `ghcr.io/ferretdb/postgres-documentdb:17-0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0`) and explain how to verify compatibility via the engine image tag suffix.

**`document-store-docs` — Verified tenancy model documented without false isolation guarantees**
The system SHALL state: shared backing Postgres DB; app-layer `tenantId` scoping (`applyTenantScopeToFilter` / `injectTenantIntoDocument`) authoritative; RLS as hardening; per-tenant DocumentDB role does NOT constitute isolation; hard isolation requires dedicated DocumentDB instance per tier.

**`document-store-docs` — Deployment topology and bundled extensions documented**
The system SHALL document: dedicated Postgres instance; colocated topology rejected; engine-first startup; bundled extensions pgvector 0.8.1, PostGIS 3.6.0, rum 1.3, pg_cron 1.6.

**`document-store-docs` — Compatibility-differences and remediations table**
The system SHALL include a table covering: no change streams (pgoutput/logical-replication as remediation direction; owning change `add-ferretdb-realtime-cdc-remediation`); no multi-document transactions (idempotent single-doc writes recommended); aggregation policy (all 15 adapter-allowed stages supported; `$out`/`$merge` blocked by adapter allowlist — policy, not engine limitation).

**`document-store-docs` — Licensing rationale recorded**
The system SHALL include a licensing section stating FerretDB (Apache-2.0) and DocumentDB extension (MIT); naming MongoDB (SSPL) as the eliminated alternative; cross-linking ADR-14.

**`document-store-docs` — MongoDB references retired**
The system SHALL not reference MongoDB as the active document store in any repository documentation file (README, architecture diagrams, prose docs, runbooks).

### Top-level tasks

1. Prerequisites and Scope Discovery (confirm sibling change design.md stability; locate docs canonical path; grep MongoDB references; find diagram sources)
2. Retire MongoDB References (README, architecture diagram, other docs; re-verify grep after)
3. Author FerretDB+DocumentDB Architecture and Operations Runbook (`docs-site/architecture/ferretdb.md`) — two-layer design; pinned pair + upgrade order; PostgreSQL prerequisites; verified tenancy model (shared DB, app-layer scoping authoritative, RLS hardening, no role isolation, dedicated-instance hard isolation); deployment topology + bundled extensions; compatibility-differences table (change streams / pgoutput, transactions / idempotent writes, aggregation / adapter-allowlist policy); change-stream remediation cross-ref; observability; licensing
4. Cross-Link ADR-14 (ADR index → runbook; runbook → ADR-14)
5. Verify Acceptance Criteria (all sections present; bidirectional ADR-14 links; compatibility table accurate; MongoDB grep clean; licensing note; observability coverage)

### Code evidence

- `apps/control-plane/src/runtime/mongodb-data-api.mjs` — `applyTenantScopeToFilter` / `injectTenantIntoDocument` (authoritative app-layer tenantId scoping)
- `apps/control-plane/src/runtime/realtime-executor.mjs:54,66` — `collMod changeStreamPreAndPostImages` + `collection.watch()` → CommandNotSupported(115) / UnknownBsonField(40415) on FerretDB 2.7.0 (basis for change-stream remediation section)
- `services/gateway-config/public-route-catalog.json` — wired route surface for document store

### Resolution (OpenSpec)

```
/opsx:apply add-ferretdb-document-store-docs
/opsx:verify add-ferretdb-document-store-docs
bash tests/blackbox/run.sh
/opsx:archive add-ferretdb-document-store-docs
```

items.title: [Note] AI Engineer
items.body:
## AI Engineer 能力地圖：Frame × 關鍵字

以下以每個 frame 作為領域；每個關鍵字一列，欄位固定為一句話理解、概念、技術、實作、情境、注意；「一句話理解」以 Full Stack 工程師熟悉的系統開發視角說明。

### Data Engineering

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETL / ELT | 像後端資料搬運管線：抽取資料、整理格式，再送進分析系統。 | 把來源資料可靠地送到分析層；ETL先轉換、ELT先落地再轉換。 | 批次/增量、CDC、schema evolution、Spark/dbt。 | 以Airflow排程、dbt轉換、資料品質檢查與重跑機制落地。 | 報表、數據同步、資料湖到倉庫。 | 避免全量重跑；處理重複、遲到資料、PII與schema變更。 |
| Data Warehouse | 專門給報表與分析查詢的集中式資料庫。 | 面向分析的集中式資料儲存，重視一致性與查詢效能。 | 星型模型、分區、columnar storage、OLAP。 | 建立raw/staging/mart分層與維度/事實表。 | BI、KPI、跨來源報表。 | 不要把交易庫直接當分析庫；控管成本與資料新鮮度。 |
| Data Lake / Lakehouse | 像大型物件儲存倉庫，但加上可查詢、版本與治理能力。 | 保留大量原始資料並兼顧治理與分析能力。 | Object storage、Parquet、Delta/Iceberg、schema-on-read。 | 以bronze/silver/gold分層，設定catalog、partition與compact。 | 半結構化資料、ML訓練、歷史留存。 | 小檔案與無治理會拖垮查詢；需管理版本、權限與生命週期。 |
| Streaming / Real-time | 把資料當事件即時處理，類似 WebSocket 或 queue consumer。 | 資料事件產生後即時處理，而非等待批次窗口。 | Kafka/PubSub、Flink/Spark Streaming、watermark、幂等。 | 設計topic/schema、consumer group、checkpoint與DLQ。 | 即時告警、推薦、即時儀表板。 | 至少一次不等於不重複；處理順序、背壓、遲到事件與重放。 |
| Data Modeling | 替資料設計可長期維護的 schema、關聯與統計口徑。 | 把業務實體、關係與指標轉成可查詢且可演進的結構。 | 正規化/反正規化、維度建模、SCD、data contract。 | 先定義grain，再建立主鍵、外鍵、指標與欄位字典。 | 跨團隊共用資料、報表與特徵。 | grain不清會造成重複計算；避免只為當下報表硬編模型。 |
| Data Quality & Governance | 替資料加上測試、ownership、權限與可追溯性。 | 確保資料正確、完整、及時、可追溯且有人負責。 | 契約測試、expectations、lineage、catalog、SLA。 | 在pipeline加入schema、null、範圍、freshness與異常告警。 | 重要報表、監管資料、ML輸入。 | 品質規則要可執行；告警過多會被忽略，需訂責任人與處置流程。 |
| Orchestration | 像 CI/CD workflow，負責安排資料任務的順序、重試與排程。 | 管理資料工作流的依賴、重試、排程與可觀測性。 | DAG、Airflow/Dagster、sensor、backfill、retry。 | 任務保持冪等，設定timeout、重試、依賴與失敗通知。 | 多步ETL、每日報表、模型pipeline。 | 不要把業務邏輯塞進排程器；避免隱性依賴與無限重試。 |

### RAG / LLM Application

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture | 把 ingestion、搜尋、LLM 與 API 拆成有清楚邊界的服務。 | 定義RAG元件如何串接、資料流如何走，以及同步/非同步邊界。 | Retriever-generator pipeline、API gateway、cache、queue。 | 拆 ingestion、retrieval、generation、evaluation 與 serving。 | 企業知識問答、客服、文件搜尋。 | 先定義延遲、成本、權限與失敗降級，再選框架。 |
| Chunking | 把長文件切成模型搜尋得到、又看得懂的小段落。 | 把文件切成適合檢索與模型上下文的片段。 | 固定長度、語意切分、recursive splitter、overlap。 | 依標題/段落切分，保留metadata並用檢索指標調整大小。 | 長文件問答、規章與技術文件。 | 切太小失去上下文，切太大降低召回；不要切斷表格與程式碼。 |
| Embedding | 把文字轉成可比較相似度的數字向量。 | 將文字轉成向量，讓語意相近內容在向量空間靠近。 | Transformer embedding、cosine similarity、批次embedding。 | 固定模型與版本，建立向量索引並記錄embedding model。 | 語意搜尋、相似案例、RAG召回。 | 模型換版需重建索引；多語、領域詞與向量維度要驗證。 |
| Vector DB | 替 embedding 建索引，讓系統能快速做語意搜尋。 | 儲存與查詢向量及其metadata的資料庫。 | HNSW/IVF、ANN、top-k、filter、Qdrant/pgvector/Milvus。 | 建立collection、索引、metadata filter與刪除/更新流程。 | 大量文件的語意檢索。 | top-k不是品質保證；注意索引更新、租戶隔離與查詢成本。 |
| Metadata Filtering | 像 SQL WHERE，先用權限、租戶或日期縮小搜尋範圍。 | 先用結構化條件縮小可檢索範圍，再做語意搜尋。 | 欄位filter、ACL filter、tenant_id、時間/版本條件。 | 把權限與來源metadata寫入chunk，檢索時強制套用。 | 依部門、產品、日期、權限搜尋。 | filter不能由模型自由決定；缺metadata會造成越權或漏召回。 |
| Hybrid Search | 同時跑關鍵字搜尋和語意搜尋，再合併結果。 | 結合關鍵字精確匹配與向量語意匹配。 | BM25、dense retrieval、rank fusion、RRF。 | 並行查詢兩路召回後融合、去重並評估權重。 | 專有名詞、編號與自然語言混合查詢。 | 只用向量容易漏掉ID/術語；融合權重需用資料驗證。 |
| Reranker | 像搜尋結果的第二輪排序器，把真正相關的內容往前排。 | 對初步召回結果重新排序，提升前幾筆相關性。 | Cross-encoder、Cohere rerank、top-N reranking。 | 先取較大的candidate pool，再對前N筆重排。 | 召回很多但答案常不在前幾筆。 | 會增加延遲與成本；不要把reranker當作權限層。 |
| Query Rewriting | 把使用者模糊的問題改寫成更容易查到資料的查詢。 | 把模糊、口語或多輪問題改寫成更適合檢索的查詢。 | Query expansion、multi-query、HyDE、conversation rewrite。 | 保留原問題，產生候選查詢並記錄改寫結果。 | 追問、省略主詞、跨語言與複雜問題。 | 改寫可能改變原意；需防止注入與錯誤擴張。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |
| Faithfulness | 檢查答案是否真的有文件證據支持。 | 答案是否能被提供的上下文支持，而非模型自行捏造。 | Citation checking、NLI、LLM-as-judge、groundedness。 | 要求引用來源，逐句比對claim與context並設拒答門檻。 | 法規、客服、內部知識問答。 | 有引用不代表真的支持；避免把judge分數當絕對真值。 |
| Hallucination | 模型講得很像真的，但內容其實沒有依據。 | 模型產生與證據不符或不存在的內容。 | Grounding、temperature control、answer abstention、fact check。 | 無證據時拒答，輸出引用與信心，記錄錯誤案例回歸。 | 資料不完整或問題超出知識庫。 | 降低temperature無法根治；需改善召回與輸出驗證。 |
| Failure Modes | 列出系統會怎麼壞，並預先設計偵測、降級與復原。 | 系統在資料、檢索、模型、工具或網路異常下的失敗型態。 | Failure taxonomy、chaos test、timeout、retry、DLQ。 | 建立錯誤分類、fallback、告警與可重現測試案例。 | 上線前演練與事故分析。 | 只測happy path不夠；重試可能放大流量與費用。 |

### Agent

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workflow | 像後端狀態機，把 Agent 任務拆成可控制的步驟。 | 把Agent任務拆成可追蹤、可重試、可控的步驟。 | State machine、DAG、LangGraph、workflow engine。 | 明確定義節點輸入輸出、轉移條件與終止條件。 | 多步研究、客服處理、資料操作。 | 避免讓模型自行決定所有流程；限制迴圈與最大步數。 |
| Tool Calling | 讓模型用結構化參數呼叫 API，而不是只產生文字。 | 讓模型以結構化參數呼叫外部工具完成工作。 | Function calling、JSON schema、tool registry。 | 驗證參數、套用權限、執行工具並把結果回傳模型。 | 查詢API、寄信、寫入資料庫。 | 工具呼叫等同權限操作；需白名單、審計與人工核准。 |
| State | 保存 Agent 做到哪裡、拿到什麼結果，以及下一步要做什麼。 | 保存Agent在多步任務中的上下文、結果與目前階段。 | State schema、checkpoint、短期/長期記憶。 | 用明確schema儲存狀態，支援重試、恢復與版本遷移。 | 長流程、多輪對話、非同步任務。 | 不要把所有對話無限塞進prompt；避免狀態污染與競態。 |
| Planning | 讓 Agent 先拆任務再執行，但每一步仍要驗證。 | 先決定子任務與執行順序，再逐步完成目標。 | ReAct、plan-and-execute、task decomposition。 | 限制計畫深度，逐步驗證工具結果並允許重新規劃。 | 研究、複合查詢、跨系統流程。 | 計畫不是事實；每一步都需驗證，並防止無限重新規劃。 |
| Guardrails | 像 middleware 與 policy layer，限制模型與工具能做什麼。 | 在輸入、工具、輸出各階段限制Agent可做的事。 | Policy engine、schema validation、content filter、allowlist。 | 建立前置/後置檢查，違規時拒絕、修正或轉人工。 | 高風險自動化、金融、客服。 | 只做輸出過濾不夠；工具層和資料層也要防護。 |
| Human-in-the-loop | 高風險動作先停住，交給人核准後才繼續。 | 在高風險或不確定步驟由人審核、接管或核准。 | Approval gate、confidence threshold、escalation。 | 設計待審佇列、審核理由、逾時與回滾流程。 | 付款、刪除、對外發信、敏感回答。 | 人工介入點要可量化；避免所有案件都卡在人工作業。 |
| Structured Output | 要求模型回傳符合 JSON Schema 的資料，方便程式接續處理。 | 要求模型輸出可被程式可靠解析的固定結構。 | JSON schema、Pydantic、constrained decoding。 | 解析後做schema與業務規則驗證，失敗則修復或重試。 | API回應、分類、工作流節點。 | 格式正確不代表內容正確；限制欄位長度與注入內容。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |

### Multi-tenant

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-tenant Architecture | 同一套後端服務多家公司，但每家的資料與資源必須隔離。 | 同一平台服務多個租戶，同時共享效率與隔離安全。 | Shared service、tenant context、quota、policy。 | 每個request注入tenant context，所有資料與快取操作強制帶租戶。 | SaaS型AI平台。 | 租戶邊界必須端到端驗證，不能只靠前端參數。 |
| Tenant Isolation | 確保任何查詢、快取、檔案與向量都不會跨租戶。 | 防止一個租戶讀寫另一個租戶的資料與資源。 | Logical/physical isolation、ACL、RLS、network policy。 | 在資料庫、快取、向量庫、物件儲存與日誌都套隔離。 | 共享基礎設施的SaaS。 | 要測越權與錯誤租戶context；背景任務也要帶tenant。 |
| Tenant ID | 像 request context 的主鍵，必須一路帶過 API、DB、queue 與 log。 | 識別請求所屬租戶並貫穿整個資料流。 | JWT claims、request context、composite key。 | 由可信身份來源取得，寫入資料表、trace、queue與cache key。 | 多租戶API與非同步工作。 | 不可信任使用者自行傳入的tenant_id；防止IDOR。 |
| Shared Database / Shared Schema | 所有租戶共用表，用 tenant_id 與 RLS 做隔離。 | 所有租戶共用資料庫與schema，以成本換取隔離複雜度。 | tenant_id、RLS、composite index、partition。 | 所有表加tenant_id，Repository層強制篩選並做隔離測試。 | 大量小租戶、成本敏感SaaS。 | 漏一個where就可能資料外洩；索引與熱租戶需特別處理。 |
| Database per Tenant | 每個租戶一個資料庫，隔離更強但維運成本更高。 | 每個租戶使用獨立資料庫，隔離與客製化較強。 | Database provisioning、migration orchestration、connection pool。 | 自動建立/升級/備份資料庫並管理租戶路由。 | 少量大型或合規租戶。 | 運維與連線成本高；migration與跨租戶分析更複雜。 |
| Row-Level Security | 讓資料庫本身強制每列資料能被哪個租戶看到。 | 由資料庫在每一列層級強制租戶存取政策。 | PostgreSQL RLS、session context、policy。 | 交易開始設定tenant context，並測試直接SQL與服務帳號路徑。 | 共享schema的強制隔離。 | 繞過RLS的管理連線很危險；政策需納入migration與測試。 |
| Tenant-aware API | API 從驗證到查詢都必須知道目前是哪個租戶。 | API在授權、資料查詢與回應中都理解租戶邊界。 | JWT、middleware、OPA、quota。 | middleware解析tenant，服務層拒絕不一致context並套用配額。 | 多租戶REST/GraphQL服務。 | 不要只在controller過濾；內部服務與webhook也要驗證。 |
| Multi-tenant Scaling | 避免單一大租戶吃光資源，並能依租戶分片、限流與擴容。 | 在租戶數、流量與資料量成長時維持隔離與效能。 | Quota、sharding、partition、autoscaling、noisy-neighbor control。 | 依租戶分片/限流，監控單租戶資源與升級路徑。 | SaaS成長與大型租戶加入。 | 平均容量會掩蓋熱租戶；需壓測最壞分布。 |

### Architecture

> 來源：Miro board 的 10 個 frame；內容以 Full Stack 工程師理解 AI 工程能力地圖為目標整理。

## AI 系統從建置到上線：三段流程

閱讀順序只有三段：**先準備資料 → 再處理使用者請求 → 最後用線上結果持續改善**。底部三項是每個階段都必須具備的系統能力。

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph PREP["A. 事前準備：把資料變成 AI 可用的知識"]
    direction LR
    DE["1. Data Engineering<br/>收集、清理、治理資料"]
    DS["2. Data Science<br/>分析資料、定義指標與特徵"]
    ML["3. ML 基礎<br/>選模型、Embedding 與推論方式"]
    KB[("可檢索知識庫<br/>Chunks + Metadata + Vectors")]
    DE --> DS --> ML --> KB
  end

  subgraph REQUEST["B. 線上請求：使用者問問題時，系統實際怎麼跑"]
    direction LR
    USER["使用者 / 前端"] --> API["API 接收問題"]
    API --> RAG["4. RAG / LLM Application<br/>找資料、排序、組 Prompt"]
    RAG --> NEED{"需要執行動作？"}
    NEED -->|否| ANSWER["LLM 產生答案"]
    NEED -->|是| AGENT["5. Agent<br/>規劃步驟、呼叫工具、保存狀態"]
    AGENT --> ANSWER
    ANSWER --> USER
  end

  KB -->|提供相關資料| RAG

  subgraph IMPROVE["C. 上線後：觀察結果並持續改善"]
    direction LR
    OBS["6. Production AI / Observability<br/>記錄品質、延遲、成本與錯誤"]
    EVAL["7. LLM Evaluation<br/>Golden Dataset、Judge、Faithfulness"]
    FIX["修正資料 / Prompt / 模型 / 流程"]
    OBS --> EVAL --> FIX
  end

  ANSWER -->|留下 Trace 與 Feedback| OBS
  FIX -->|重新發佈| RAG
  FIX -->|補資料與品質規則| DE

  CROSS["所有階段共同要求<br/>8. Multi-tenant：租戶與資料隔離<br/>9. AI Security / Reliability：權限、PII、Guardrails<br/>10. Architecture：Queue、Cache、Scaling、Fault Tolerance"]
```

items.title: 工程脚手架：Connector SPI 多模块 + Flink/SeaTunnel 作业骨架（可独立运行）
items.body:
## 背景

为 `data-foundation` 建立**可独立开发 / 编译 / 调试 / 运行**的工程脚手架——数据底座（流批采集 + 湖仓 + 统一计算 + Connector SPI）。核心是把 **Connector SPI** 的"加插件不动主干"骨架先立起来（信创刚需收敛点）。

> 依赖：主仓 [libs-java HashMatrixData/hashmatrix#1](https://github.com/HashMatrixData/hashmatrix/issues/1)；设计见架构 [03-技术选型](https://github.com/HashMatrixData/hashmatrix/blob/main/docs/architecture/03-技术选型.md) / [04-工程与部署](https://github.com/HashMatrixData/hashmatrix/blob/main/docs/architecture/04-工程与部署.md)。

## 任务清单（DoD）

**Maven 多模块（独立可构建运行）**
- [ ] `connector-spi/`：定义 SPI 接口（连接 / 元数据扫描 / 读写）
- [ ] `connector-jdbc/`：标准 JDBC **参考实现**（PostgreSQL/MySQL）
- [ ] `connector-dialect-*/`：达梦 / 人大金仓 / OceanBase 方言插件**占位**（**新增数据库 = 加一个插件 jar，不改主干**）
- [ ] `ingest/`：Flink + Flink-CDC（流）/ SeaTunnel（批）作业**骨架**（本地 mini-cluster 可跑）
- [ ] `app/`：服务骨架，`<parent>` + `import` BOM + `starter-tenant`（**Maven 坐标引用**）；**只 clone 本仓即可 `mvn package`**

**多租户与配额**
- [ ] 采集 / 计算 / 湖仓**按租户隔离 catalog/database**（Doris/Paimon per-tenant）；作业受租户配额约束

**测试与 Mock**
- [ ] 复用 `starter-test`；Connector SPI 契约测试（参考实现）；**Mock 数据脱敏**（`acme`/`tenant-demo`）
- [ ] Flink 作业本地集成测试（Testcontainers / mini-cluster）

**本地独立运行/调试**
- [ ] `docker-compose.local.yml`（PG + MinIO + 可选 Doris/Kafka）；`Dockerfile`；健康检查通过

**交付汇入**
- [ ] Helm 子 chart 占位到主仓 `deploy/charts/data-foundation` → 关联 HashMatrixData/hashmatrix#2
- [ ] CI：多模块构建 + 测试 + 镜像

## 边界

- **数据采集（本仓·主链路·搬行数据）≠ 元数据采集（`governance`·旁路·取结构）（AD-15）**：二者**共用 Connector SPI + 数据源统一管理**，连接器只实现一次。

## 约束

- 🔴 红线见 `CLAUDE.md`（公开仓，禁甲方信息，示例脱敏）。

## 验收

只 clone 本仓 → `mvn package`（多模块）通过 → `connector-jdbc` 契约测试绿 → `docker-compose up` + Flink 样例本地跑通。

items.title: Epic: establish document processing business package
items.body:
## Goal

Introduce a complete, hostable `@accounterbro/document-processing` business package that owns the tenant-scoped lifecycle and persisted result of processing a registered document.

This Epic deliberately stops at the business-package boundary. It does not create a new service or messaging integration. The package must be independently complete so a later service can orchestrate ObjectStorage/extraction and invoke the package through the existing execution runtime.

Epic branch: `epic-document-processing-package`.

## Context

AccounterBro already has `@accounterbro/documents`, which owns document registration and emits `DocumentRegisteredEvent` after successful registration. A future Document Processing service is expected to react to that fact, obtain the document binary through ObjectStorage, run an extractor, and record the processing result.

That future orchestration is intentionally not part of this Epic. The first step is to establish the business model and execution/persistence contracts that the future service will host.

`packages/documents` is the canonical working reference for a business feature package that owns domain state plus EDP Operations, Reads, handlers, persistence, execution bindings, TypeORM composition and a runtime manifest. Follow its proven responsibility boundaries and public-entrypoint structure where applicable; do not mechanically copy Documents-specific fields, registration semantics or service behavior.

Repository instructions remain authoritative:

- root `AGENTS.md` for workspace workflow, Nx/generator usage, boundaries and verification;
- `packages/AGENTS.md` for package routing and the Documents reference;
- `docs/engineering/package-guidelines.md` for business-package domain, execution, tenant, event, persistence and runtime-manifest rules.

## Package boundary

The Epic establishes:

```text
packages/document-processing/
  src/
    index.ts
    execution.ts
    typeorm.ts
    runtime.ts
    lib/
      document-processing/
      operations/
      reads/
      events/
      ports/
      persistence/typeorm/
```

The public boundaries follow the existing business-package pattern:

- root entrypoint: business-facing contracts and runtime values required by consumers;
- `/execution`: package-owned handler construction descriptors and Operation/Read binding groups;
- `/typeorm`: package-owned entities, migrations, persistence token/factory and schema composition contracts;
- `/runtime`: one framework-agnostic manifest aggregating the package's execution and TypeORM contributions.

The package must not depend on `@accounterbro/documents`. Cross-domain identities and references come from `@accounterbro/core`.

## Domain model

The package owns a `DocumentProcessing` aggregate representing processing of one registered Document for one tenant.

Conceptual state:

```text
DocumentProcessing
├── id: DocumentProcessingId
├── tenantId: TenantId
├── documentId: DocumentId
├── status: PENDING | COMPLETED | FAILED
├── extractedText?: string
└── failureReason?: string
```

`DocumentProcessingId` is a separate aggregate identity. `DocumentId` is a cross-domain reference to the source document, not the identity of the processing aggregate.

The persistence model enforces at most one processing aggregate for a given `(tenant_id, document_id)` pair. This is tenant-local business deduplication and must not be treated as a replacement for EDP execution idempotency.

Allowed state transitions are intentionally small:

```text
PENDING -> COMPLETED
PENDING -> FAILED
```

A completed processing stores extracted text. A failed processing stores a failure reason. Aggregate construction/restore owns valid state shape and transition invariants.

## Execution model

### Prepare document processing

`PrepareDocumentProcessingOperation` creates a `PENDING` processing aggregate or returns the existing aggregate for the same tenant/document pair.

Its payload contains the new processing identity and source `DocumentId`. Its result distinguishes `created` from `existing` so repeated future orchestration can reuse the existing business state.

### Finish document processing

`FinishDocumentProcessingOperation` finishes an existing `PENDING` aggregate with one of two outcomes:

- `completed` with extracted text;
- `failed` with a failure reason.

The aggregate owns the transition invariant; the handler owns orchestration through tenant-scoped persistence.

### Get document processing

`GetDocumentProcessingRead` is tenant-aware and retrieves processing state by `DocumentId`, returning the processing identity, source document identity, status and the state-appropriate result/failure data.

## Event model

Successful processing is a business fact that may drive a later downstream feature. The package therefore owns `DocumentProcessingCompletedEvent`.

The event is returned by `FinishDocumentProcessingHandler` through the successful `OperationResult` after the state change has been persisted through the package boundary, following the producer-side pattern already proven by Documents. EDP Runner remains responsible for event-envelope creation, transaction coordination and Outbox persistence.

Initial event payload:

```text
{
  processingId: DocumentProcessingId,
  documentId: DocumentId
}
```

Do not put `extractedText` into the event. The event communicates that processing completed; it is not a transport for potentially large extracted document content. Execution metadata already owned by the EDP event envelope must not be duplicated into the business payload without a concrete requirement.

The initial package does not emit `DocumentProcessingFailedEvent`. `FAILED` is persisted business state. A failure event should be introduced only when a concrete downstream consumer requires that business fact.

## Tenant ownership and persistence

Document Processing is tenant-owned.

All applicable Operations, Reads, handlers and persistence calls must use the tenant-aware EDP contracts and explicit tenant scope required by the repository package guidance. Persistence lookup and mutation predicates must enforce tenant isolation rather than loading globally and checking ownership afterward.

The database owns tenant-local uniqueness for `(tenant_id, document_id)` and any other invariant that repository guidance assigns to the database boundary. Aggregate state/transition validity remains owned by the aggregate and restore/mapping boundary rather than being duplicated mechanically in schema policy.

## Explicitly out of scope

- a `document-processing` service under `apps/services/`;
- consuming `DocumentRegisteredEvent`;
- broker/CDC/consumer/runtime transport work;
- ObjectStorage read support;
- OCR, AI or another concrete extractor;
- a `DocumentExtractor` service/application port;
- HTTP presenters/endpoints;
- structured invoice/expense/accounting interpretation such as merchant, amount, currency, VAT or category;
- retry/recovery orchestration outside the existing EDP execution guarantees;
- changes to `@accounterbro/documents` except if a concrete compatibility defect is discovered and separately justified.

The first completed result is intentionally only `extractedText: string`.

## Planned task order

The Epic is implemented through small sequential tasks. Each code-changing task uses its own branch created from the latest Epic branch and a PR targeting `epic-document-processing-package`.

1. #290 — Add Document Processing identity and reference contracts to Core.
2. #291 — Create Document Processing package and domain model.
3. #292 — Add Document Processing execution, read and completion event contracts.
4. #293 — Add Document Processing TypeORM persistence and runtime composition.

## Acceptance criteria

- `@accounterbro/core` exposes the Document Processing name, branded ID and aggregate reference required by the new business package;
- `@accounterbro/document-processing` exists as a repository-generated `type:business` Nx package;
- the package owns a tenant-scoped `DocumentProcessing` aggregate with `PENDING`, `COMPLETED` and `FAILED` invariants;
- one processing aggregate per `(tenant, document)` is enforced by persistence/database semantics;
- prepare execution creates or returns existing processing state without depending on Documents internals;
- finish execution supports completed and failed outcomes and rejects invalid state transitions at the aggregate boundary;
- successful finish emits `DocumentProcessingCompletedEvent` with `processingId` and `documentId` and does not include extracted text or duplicate envelope-owned metadata;
- failed finish persists `FAILED` without emitting a speculative failure event;
- a tenant-aware Read returns processing state by `DocumentId`;
- persistence and mapping round-trip valid aggregate states while tenant isolation and tenant-local uniqueness are enforced at their owning database boundaries;
- `/execution`, `/typeorm` and `/runtime` expose the same proven package responsibilities as the canonical Documents reference where those responsibilities apply;
- package tests cover aggregate invariants, handler behavior, tenant-scoped persistence, database uniqueness and package composition at their owning boundaries;
- the Epic introduces no service, transport, ObjectStorage read, extractor or HTTP behavior.

## Definition of Done

- all planned task issues are complete or explicitly removed/revised from scope with a concrete reason;
- every task PR is merged into `epic-document-processing-package` only after its repository-defined checks, acceptance criteria and required review are satisfied;
- the combined Epic diff remains within the Core + Document Processing package boundary described above;
- the final package is hostable through the existing `@accounterbro/runtime-executions` manifest composition without service-local handler/persistence reconstruction;
- relevant full repository-required CI is green on the final Epic branch;
- final Epic review confirms the package follows current repository instructions and uses Documents only as a canonical responsibility reference, not as a mechanically copied domain template;
- only then is the Epic branch eligible to merge into `main`.

items.title: Deploy the FerretDB gateway: stateless MongoDB wire endpoint, horizontal scaling, TLS, internal-only
items.body:
> Updated to reconcile with ADR-14 spike findings (PR #467). Source of truth: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-gateway/`.

## Problem

Falcone's document store reaches MongoDB via `MONGO_URI`, resolved in
`apps/control-plane/src/runtime/main.mjs::mongoUri` (line 33). MongoDB's SSPL
licence is incompatible with Falcone's open-source model. FerretDB v2 is the selected
replacement (ADR-14, `add-ferretdb-adr-spike`): it speaks the MongoDB wire protocol
and translates to SQL against a PostgreSQL 17 + DocumentDB engine backend. Before
Falcone's client can be repointed, the FerretDB gateway process must be deployed
in-cluster as a stateless, horizontally scalable component reachable only by Falcone's
control-plane and CDC services.

## Why / What Changes

### Why

The FerretDB gateway (`ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb:2.7.0`, Apache-2.0) is a stateless
process that speaks MongoDB wire protocol 7.0 (maxWireVersion 21, buildInfo 7.0.77)
and translates operations to SQL against the DocumentDB-on-Postgres backend deployed
by `add-ferretdb-documentdb-engine` (#456). It must be deployed and proven operational
in-cluster before `MONGO_URI` is repointed (separate child
`add-ferretdb-data-access-cutover`).

### What Changes

- Add a Kubernetes Deployment for the FerretDB gateway image pinned by **tag + digest**:
  `ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb:2.7.0@sha256:5706414241eb84f0515512c37b46db0f1b1eac9e5ceb7e4c2523211c184b1985`
  to the umbrella chart, gated by `ferretdb.enabled` so it can be deployed alongside
  MongoDB during the cutover window.
- Configure the Deployment with a minimum of 2 replicas, no PVC (stateless), and
  HPA-ready resource requests/limits.
- Expose an internal `mongodb://` ClusterIP Service (port 27017); no Ingress, Route,
  NodePort, or LoadBalancer.
- Point the gateway at the DocumentDB-on-Postgres backend via `FERRETDB_POSTGRESQL_URL`
  with `sslmode=require`.
- Configure `FERRETDB_POSTGRESQL_URL` to use the **bootstrap/superuser** Postgres
  role for the gateway's own backend connection. Per-tenant MongoDB users created via
  `db.runCommand({createUser})` map to real **non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS** Postgres
  login roles in the DocumentDB backend — provisioned by
  `add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials` (#458).
- Configure health and readiness probes (HTTP `/debug/healthz` on port 8088 or TCP
  on port 27017).
- Enforce the **engine-first startup contract:** the DocumentDB engine MUST be started
  (extensions initialised, `documentdb_api` schema present) BEFORE the FerretDB gateway
  process; starting the gateway first causes the first wire handshake to fail. Implement
  via an initContainer or readiness gate from `add-ferretdb-documentdb-engine`.
- Pin the gateway image tag and digest to the version corresponding to engine
  `0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0`; chart values MUST include a comment documenting
  wire protocol (MongoDB 7.0, maxWireVersion 21, buildInfo 7.0.77) and the
  engine-first upgrade order.
- Apply OpenShift restricted-v2 SCC compliance (`runAsNonRoot: true`,
  `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`, no explicit `fsGroup`) in
  `deploy/openshift/values-openshift.yaml`.
- Add Harbor pull-secret annotation and airgap image-rewrite stanza for
  `ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb` in the OpenShift overlay.

**CRITICAL NON-GOAL — tenant isolation boundary:** the FerretDB gateway at v2.7.0
does NOT enforce per-database role scoping. An authenticated MongoDB user can read
other Mongo databases. The per-tenant DB + role model provisioned by
`add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials` (#458) is NOT a DB-level isolation
boundary at this version. Tenant isolation MUST remain enforced at the application
layer (`apps/control-plane/src/runtime/mongodb-data-api.mjs` tenantId scoping). The
gateway MUST NOT be presented to operators as a tenant isolation boundary.

## Spec Delta (EARS — `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-gateway/specs/data-api/spec.md`)

ADDED Requirements:

1. **FerretDB gateway deployed as a stateless Deployment via chart toggle** — The system SHALL deploy the FerretDB gateway as a stateless Deployment (>=2 replicas, no PVC, HPA-ready) controlled by `ferretdb.enabled`.
2. **FerretDB gateway exposes MongoDB wire protocol on internal-only ClusterIP Service** — port 27017, no Ingress/Route/NodePort/LoadBalancer; wire handshake returns `maxWireVersion: 21` and `buildInfo.version: "7.0.77"`.
3. **FerretDB gateway translates wire protocol to DocumentDB-on-Postgres backend** — via `FERRETDB_POSTGRESQL_URL` with `sslmode=require`.
4. **FerretDB gateway health and readiness probes gate Service endpoint registration** — liveness + readiness on `/debug/healthz:8088` or TCP:27017; Pod excluded from Service until ready.
5. **FerretDB gateway image version must be pinned by tag and digest** — `ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb:2.7.0@sha256:5706414241eb84f0515512c37b46db0f1b1eac9e5ceb7e4c2523211c184b1985`; chart values document wire protocol (MongoDB 7.0, maxWireVersion 21, buildInfo 7.0.77) and engine-first upgrade order.
6. **FerretDB gateway Pods comply with OpenShift restricted-v2 SCC** — `runAsNonRoot: true`, `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`, no explicit `fsGroup` in OpenShift overlay.
7. **FerretDB gateway MUST NOT become Ready before the DocumentDB engine extensions are initialised** — engine-first startup; gateway readiness gate blocks until `documentdb_api` schema exists.
8. **FerretDB gateway backend connection uses bootstrap superuser role; per-tenant MongoDB users map to non-superuser, non-BYPASSRLS Postgres login roles** — per-tenant credential provisioning is owned by `add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials` (#458).
9. **FerretDB gateway v2.7.0 does NOT provide a tenant isolation boundary — application-layer tenantId scoping is authoritative** — `mongodb-data-api.mjs` is the authoritative isolation point; cross-tenant DB reads via the gateway are a known v2.7.0 limitation.

## Tasks (`openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-gateway/tasks.md`)

- [ ] 1.1 Confirm `add-ferretdb-documentdb-engine` applied; record `FERRETDB_POSTGRESQL_URL` value pattern in design.md D1
- [ ] 1.2 Identify FerretDB 2.7.0 health endpoint port (expected 8088 for `/debug/healthz`)
- [ ] 2.1–2.4 Chart: `ferretdb.*` values stanza (image pinned by digest, `replicaCount: 2`, resources, DSN, probe config); Deployment template; ClusterIP Service template
- [ ] 3.1–3.2 Networking: internal-only enforcement; optional NetworkPolicy
- [ ] 4.1–4.2 TLS: `FERRETDB_POSTGRESQL_URL` with `sslmode=require`; defer MongoDB-protocol TLS to follow-on
- [ ] 5.1–5.3 Health + readiness probes; verify via `helm template`
- [ ] 6.1–6.3 OpenShift SCC overlay + Harbor pull-secret + image-rewrite stanza
- [ ] 7.1–7.4 Version-coupling: digest pin in values; chart comment with wire-protocol info (MongoDB 7.0, maxWireVersion 21, buildInfo 7.0.77) and engine-first upgrade order; initContainer/readiness gate for engine-first startup
- [ ] 8.1–8.7 Validation (`helm lint`, `helm template`, kind deploy, wire-protocol handshake check `maxWireVersion: 21` / `buildInfo.version: "7.0.77"`, `openspec validate --strict`, non-goal note present in design/proposal/spec, bootstrap-superuser secret sourcing)

Full checklist: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-gateway/tasks.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] FerretDB connects to the DocumentDB engine; in-cluster `mongosh`/driver smoke returns `maxWireVersion: 21` and `buildInfo.version: "7.0.77"`.
- [ ] Image in chart is pinned by both tag and digest: `ghcr.io/ferretdb/ferretdb:2.7.0@sha256:5706414241eb84f0515512c37b46db0f1b1eac9e5ceb7e4c2523211c184b1985`.
- [ ] Chart values contain a comment documenting: wire MongoDB 7.0 / maxWireVersion 21 / buildInfo 7.0.77; engine-first startup and upgrade order; paired engine image `0.107.0-ferretdb-2.7.0`.
- [ ] Gateway Deployment is stateless (no PVC), minimum 2 replicas, HPA-ready.
- [ ] ClusterIP-only Service on port 27017; no Ingress, Route, NodePort, or LoadBalancer.
- [ ] `FERRETDB_POSTGRESQL_URL` uses the bootstrap/superuser Postgres role (sourced from Secret, not hardcoded).
- [ ] Per-tenant MongoDB user maps to a Postgres role with neither `SUPERUSER` nor `BYPASSRLS` (verified via `pg_roles`).
- [ ] Engine-first startup gate: gateway Pod does not pass readiness until `documentdb_api` schema is present in the DocumentDB backend.
- [ ] Probes configured: liveness + readiness on `/debug/healthz:8088` or TCP:27017.
- [ ] OpenShift overlay: `runAsNonRoot: true`; `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`; no non-null `fsGroup`; image registry rewritten to Harbor.
- [ ] design.md, proposal.md, and spec.md all carry the CRITICAL non-goal note: "FerretDB v2.7.0 does NOT enforce per-database role scoping; tenant isolation remains authoritative at the application layer (`mongodb-data-api.mjs` tenantId scoping)"; cross-reference to `add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials` (#458) present in all three.
- [ ] `openspec validate add-ferretdb-gateway --strict` passes.

## Out of Scope

- Repointing Falcone's client (`MONGO_URI`): separate child `add-ferretdb-data-access-cutover`.
- Per-tenant DocumentDB role provisioning: `add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials` (#458).
- MongoDB-protocol TLS (gateway to client): deferred to follow-on mTLS/service-mesh change.

## Code Evidence

- `apps/control-plane/src/runtime/main.mjs::mongoUri` (line 33) — `MONGO_URI` resolution; repoint target for `add-ferretdb-data-access-cutover`
- `apps/control-plane/src/runtime/mongodb-data-api.mjs` — authoritative `tenantId` scoping; MUST remain the isolation boundary
- `charts/in-falcone/values.yaml:18-22, 137-138` — existing OpenShift SCC pattern to follow

## Dependencies

- **DEPENDS ON:** `add-ferretdb-documentdb-engine` (#456) — DocumentDB backend must be running and extensions initialised before the gateway can start.
- **BLOCKS:** `add-ferretdb-data-access-cutover` (client repoint); per-tenant DocumentDB role provisioning.
- **Cross-ref:** `add-ferretdb-tenant-isolation-credentials` (#458) for credential model and non-BYPASSRLS enforcement.

**Epic:** #454
**Siblings:** #456 (DocumentDB engine), #458 (tenant credentials), #459 (data access cutover), #460 (CDC remediation), #461 (migration validation), #462 (data migration runbook), #463 (rollback plan), #464 (docs), #465 (E2E)

---

## OpenSpec change

- Package: `openspec/changes/add-ferretdb-gateway/` — validated `openspec validate add-ferretdb-gateway --strict` ✅
- Capability spec deltas: `data-api`
- Status: **proposed** (0/23 tasks).

## Resolution (OpenSpec)

`/opsx:apply add-ferretdb-gateway` → `/opsx:verify add-ferretdb-gateway` → `bash tests/blackbox/run.sh` → `/opsx:archive add-ferretdb-gateway`

Optional real E2E: `/e2e-issue add-ferretdb-gateway`

items.title: Add "Architecture" section under Guides & References / Backend Development: monolith vs. microservices (benefits, drawbacks, when to use each), backend/frontend layering with API gateway and BFF, migration paths (legacy stack → modern, monolith → modular monolith → microservices, single-tenant → SaaS), a "starting a new project" technology guide, and a cheat sheet PDF
items.body:
## Summary

Add a new **Architecture** documentation section at **Guides & References / Backend Development**, as a sibling
of the existing Hibernate, SpringBoot, GraphQL, Spring Batch, OAuth, Quarkus, Messaging and Architectural
Patterns references (`modules/ROOT/pages/backend/architecture/`), following the exact structure/conventions of
those sections: a landing page with a **Bibliography** section, **one page per concept** explored in the two
requester-provided books (each with the disclaimer partial, a `== References` section linking the online
documentation the concept derives from, and Mermaid/SVG figures), and a one-page, printable, downloadable
**Architecture cheat sheet PDF** styled like the existing `architectural-patterns-cheat-sheet.pdf` /
`messaging-cheat-sheet.pdf`.

The section answers four questions the site does not answer today:

1. **Monolith or microservices?** — what each architectural style actually is, the **benefits** of microservices
   (independent teams and services; small, fast-to-evolve, independently deployable and scalable services;
   fault isolation; freedom to adopt new technology) and their **inconveniences** (loss of ACID transactionality
   and of globally consistent queries, distributed-system and operational complexity, far more code and
   infrastructure to maintain, cross-service feature coordination, the difficulty of finding the right service
   boundaries), and **when each one is the better choice** — monoliths for small projects, small teams, one-shot
   deliveries and applications that will not need to evolve much; microservices for large, complex, long-lived
   systems that must scale, be developed by several autonomous teams, or need per-component scaling for
   performance reasons.
2. **How to layer an architecture** so backend and frontend evolve independently: a REST (or GraphQL/gRPC) API
   behind an **API gateway** / **backends-for-frontends**, completely separate web frontends (React, Angular,
   Vue) that consume that API, and native mobile apps consuming the very same API — versus server-rendered UIs
   and when those still make sense.
3. **Migration paths** — from legacy technology stacks to modern ones, from monoliths to modular monoliths and
   to microservices (the **strangler fig** application, the three refactoring strategies, integration glue and
   anti-corruption layers, splitting the domain model and the database, sequencing extractions so the monolith
   never needs compensating transactions, adapting security), and from single-tenant installed software to
   multi-tenant **SaaS** (silo lift-and-shift, layered migration, service-by-service migration, and the
   silo/pool deployment models).
4. **Which path and which technologies to pick for a brand-new project**, chosen among the technologies already
   documented on this site, based on the expected project profile: large or small, low or high traffic, one-shot
   vs. long-term maintenance and evolution, one team vs. many, need for native apps, need for multi-tenancy.

Pages 3 and 4 (the migration paths and the "new project" guide) must be written in an **easy, simple-to-follow
style, with worked examples, Mermaid diagrams and SVG figures** and with **links to recommended external sites**
as proof of the explained concepts and as a way to obtain further information. For the other pages Mermaid/SVG
figures are not mandatory — add them only where they genuinely help.

## Context

### What already exists in this repository

Do **not** re-document these; link to them and add only what they do not cover.

| Existing page | What it already covers | Relationship to the new section |
|------|------|------|
| `backend/architectural-patterns/*` (16 pages, issue #152) | DDD applied to microservices: strategic design, bounded contexts and the context map, tactical building blocks, **why distributed transactions don't work across services**, sagas, domain events, the transactional outbox, CQRS, event sourcing. | The new section is the **macro-level** companion: it decides *whether* and *how* to go to microservices; every time a new page reaches "and then you need a saga / an outbox / a CQRS view", it links to the corresponding Architectural Patterns page instead of re-explaining it. The strategic-design page's decompose-by-subdomain content is linked from the decomposition parts of the monolith-to-microservices path. |
| `backend/springboot/architectural-patterns.adoc` | Introductory SOLID, hexagonal architecture, outbox, listen-to-yourself, saga diagram. | Hexagonal architecture per service is linked, not repeated. |
| `backend/graphql/when-to-use-graphql-or-rest.adoc`, `backend/springboot/rest-apis.adoc`, `backend/springboot/grpc-apis.adoc`, `backend/springboot/api-first-rest-and-grpc.adoc`, `backend/graphql/federation.adoc` | REST vs. GraphQL vs. gRPC trade-offs, API-first with OpenAPI/protobuf, GraphQL federation as a gateway. | The API-style choice is delegated to these pages; the layering and gateway pages only explain *where* the API sits. |
| `backend/oauth/browser-based-apps.adoc`, `backend/oauth/native-and-mobile-apps.adoc`, `backend/oauth/flows-overview.adoc` | The **BFF pattern for SPA authentication** (token-mediating backend, HttpOnly cookies), the native-app profile with PKCE. | The layering / gateway pages link here for the security side of separating frontend from backend; the migration page's "adapting the monolith's session security to tokens" section links here too. |
| `backend/quarkus/quarkus-vs-spring-boot.adoc`, `backend/springboot/java-or-kotlin.adoc`, `backend/quarkus/java-or-kotlin.adoc`, `backend/messaging/kafka-vs-rabbitmq.adoc`, `database/choosing-the-right-database.adoc`, `database/solr/solr-vs-elasticsearch.adoc` | Pairwise technology comparisons. | The "new project" guide **composes** these existing comparisons into stack recommendations per project profile and links to each of them; it never repeats their arguments. |

* `index.adoc` — "Architecture" landing page: what the section is about in one paragraph, the running example,
